### **Elevator Pitches (ready for reuse)**

**Six words:** “Dropshipping, without the coding.”

**One sentence:** “AeroDrop is the all-in-one Shopify app that finds
AliExpress products, imports them in one click, prices them
automatically and fulfills orders for you - so a merchant runs the
business instead of the busywork.”

**One paragraph:** “Most new Shopify dropshippers spend their first
weeks doing the same repetitive job over and over: finding a product on
AliExpress, copying its title, description and images into Shopify by
hand, guessing at a fair markup, and then manually re-ordering the item
from the supplier every time a customer buys it. AeroDrop replaces all
of that with one connected workflow - product discovery, one-click
import, editable drafts, rule-based pricing, automatic supplier order
placement and a live sales dashboard - so a merchant can go from a
browser tab full of research to a published, sellable, fulfillable
product in minutes, and keep scaling from their first sale to their
first thousand without adding headcount.”

# **02 - Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)**

Primary ICP: Shopify store owners, dropshipping entrepreneurs, eCommerce
business owners, online sellers, small retail brands, product hunters
and merchants sourcing products from AliExpress or similar supplier
networks.

| **Question**                        | **Answer**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Who are they?                       | Shopify store owners, dropshipping entrepreneurs, eCommerce business owners, online sellers, small retail brands, product hunters, and merchants who source products from suppliers such as AliExpress and sell through Shopify.                                                                                |
| What do they currently think?       | Dropshipping can be managed manually by searching products, copying product information, uploading images, setting prices and placing supplier orders one by one. They may assume automation becomes necessary only after the store becomes large.                                                              |
| What problem do they face?          | Too much time is spent finding products, importing details, editing descriptions, managing variants, updating prices, checking inventory, placing supplier orders, reviewing delivery status and fixing product-listing issues manually.                                                                        |
| What do we want them to think?      | AeroDrop is not only a product importer. It is a dropshipping operating platform that helps Shopify sellers find, import, edit, publish, price, manage and fulfill products from one connected workflow.                                                                                                        |
| What action do we want?             | Connect a Shopify store, explore products, import products, review draft listings, publish to the store, configure pricing rules and begin managing orders through AeroDrop.                                                                                                                                    |
| What proof will convince them?      | Shopify integration, AliExpress import, one-click publishing, product editing, order and fulfillment visibility, automatic price updates, live sales and profit dashboards, fast shipping options, AI-assisted titles and descriptions on paid plans, image-based search, multi-store support and 24/7 support. |
| What tone should we use?            | Simple, entrepreneurial, practical, time-saving, growth-focused and eCommerce-friendly. The communication should make dropshipping feel more manageable without promising guaranteed sales or effortless profit.                                                                                                |
| Which channels will influence them? | Shopify App Store, Shopify communities, Facebook eCommerce groups, YouTube tutorials, TikTok/Reels demonstrations, dropshipping communities, email campaigns, influencer reviews, comparison content, webinars and retargeting.                                                                                 |

### **Priority Buyer Segments**

| **Segment**                | **Primary Need**                                                           | **Desired Action**                                                   |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Shopify Store Owners       | Fast import, store setup, price control, stock updates, order visibility   | Connect store and import the first products                          |
| Dropshipping Entrepreneurs | Product discovery, automation, faster testing and scaling                  | Test product ideas and configure repeatable workflows                |
| eCommerce Business Owners  | Operational efficiency, product quality, margin clarity and fulfillment    | Adopt AeroDrop as the operational layer for sourcing and fulfillment |
| Small Retail Brands        | Easy setup, branded packaging, lower dependency and fast product expansion | Use product sourcing and brand-first fulfillment options             |
| Product Hunters            | Trending-product discovery, image search, demand signals and testing speed | Explore and shortlist products for store testing                     |
| AliExpress-Based Merchants | Supplier imports, variants, pricing, order placement and delivery updates  | Move supplier operations into one connected dashboard                |

### **Core Jobs to Be Done**

- Find products with enough information to make a quick listing
  decision.

- Move product information from a supplier source into Shopify without
  repetitive copying.

- Edit titles, descriptions, variants, images and prices before
  publishing.

- Keep product prices, inventory and order status organized as the store
  grows.

- Reduce routine fulfillment work so more time can be spent on marketing
  and customer acquisition.

- Build a more professional store experience through reliable delivery
  and brand-first packaging options.

### **Persona Narratives**

The table above is accurate but abstract. The three narratives below
translate it into the concrete moments AeroDrop's messaging, onboarding
and support content should be written for.

**Persona 1 - Rafiq, the First-Time Shopify Dropshipper.** Rafiq has
watched enough YouTube videos to open a Shopify store and pick a niche,
but every product research session ends the same way: twelve AliExpress
tabs open, a half-filled spreadsheet of prices, and no product actually
listed by the end of the night. His real barrier isn't ambition, it's
friction - he needs to go from “this looks like a winning product” to
“this is live on my store” in one sitting, or he loses momentum and
closes the laptop. AeroDrop's Find Products page, one-click import into
Draft Products, and Basic Pricing Rule are built exactly for this
moment: they compress research-to-listing from hours to minutes.

**Persona 2 - Nusrat, the Scaling Multi-Store Operator.** Nusrat already
runs one profitable store and is testing a second niche. Her problem is
no longer discovery, it's operations: she needs orders from both stores
to reach her supplier without her manually re-typing them, she needs
pricing rules that behave consistently across catalogs of different
sizes, and she needs a single dashboard that tells her, at a glance,
which store is actually making money this week. The Premium plan's three
connected stores, unlimited processed orders, and automated Order
Settings toggle (“Automatically place orders to supplier”) are built for
exactly this stage of growth.

**Persona 3 - The Small Retail Brand Owner Moving Off Manual Sourcing.**
This merchant already has a brand identity, a logo, a returning customer
base and a reputation to protect - dropshipping quality and delivery
speed are now brand risks, not just cost lines. Generic supplier
packaging and unpredictable shipping times are the objection that keeps
this segment away from dropshipping tools generally. AeroDrop's
messaging around “customized sourcing for unique branding” and
“brand-first fulfillment” is aimed squarely at converting this hesitant,
higher-value segment.

### **Common Objections & How AeroDrop Should Answer Them**

| **Objection**                                             | **Recommended Response Direction**                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| “I can already do this manually for free.”                | Reframe the cost as time, not money - quantify hours saved per week once a store passes roughly 20–30 SKUs, and point to the Free plan removing any financial risk in testing the claim.                           |
| “Dropshipping apps all look the same.”                    | Lead with the specific combined workflow - discovery + import + editing + automated supplier ordering + live dashboard in one place - rather than any single feature, since the combination is the differentiator. |
| “Will my margins survive supplier price changes?”         | Point to the automatic price-update capability and the Pricing Rules engine (Basic and Standard/tiered rules) that recalculates the storefront price whenever product cost changes.                                |
| “Will shipping times hurt my customer reviews?”           | Be specific and qualified rather than absolute - reference access to suppliers offering faster global shipping, without promising a universal delivery window (see Section 16, Claims & Compliance Guardrails).    |
| “I don't want to be locked into a plan I don't need yet.” | Emphasize that plan changes take effect immediately in both directions (upgrade or downgrade) per the in-app Pricing Plan FAQ.                                                                                     |

# **03 - Brand Guideline**

### **Logo**


*Primary AeroDrop wordmark - captured live from the application header.*

**Primary name:** AeroDrop

**Descriptor:** All-in-One Shopify Dropshipping Platform

**Logo direction:** Use the supplied horizontal logo as the primary
mark. Keep the original orange and graphite construction, preserve
proportions and use it on white or very light backgrounds whenever
possible. A symbol-only version (the stylized “7/arrow” form inside the
second “O”) should be used only when approved artwork is available.

**Clear space:** Maintain generous clear space around the logo.
Recommended working standard: at least the height of the letter “O”
around all sides. Final master-grid approval is required before
publishing a formal logo manual.

**Minimum size:** Recommended working standard: 150 px wide for digital
and 38 mm wide for print. Confirm legibility through real application
testing before treating this as an official minimum.

**Incorrect usage:** Do not stretch, rotate, recolour, crop, add
shadows, separate the arrow element, change letter spacing, or place the
logo on busy backgrounds.

**Logo asset source:**
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Q2OoMLekt6oUa04VkZkNwluhrDVoZM4w?usp=drive_link

### **Brand Purpose, Mission, Vision & Values**

| **Element**   | **Guideline**                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Brand purpose | Make dropshipping operations easier for Shopify sellers by reducing repetitive product sourcing, listing and fulfillment work.                                                                          |
| Mission       | Provide an accessible Shopify dropshipping platform that connects product discovery, importing, editing, pricing, order handling, fulfillment visibility and growth insights in one practical workflow. |
| Vision        | Help more entrepreneurs build scalable eCommerce businesses without being limited by repetitive supplier and store-management work.                                                                     |
| Core values   | Simplicity, entrepreneurship, practical automation, speed, transparency, merchant growth, reliable support and continuous improvement.                                                                  |
| Brand promise | AeroDrop helps merchants spend less time on repetitive dropshipping operations and more time building their store, brand and customer base.                                                             |
| Key message   | One connected dropshipping platform for sourcing, listing and fulfillment.                                                                                                                              |

### **Brand Positioning**

| **Positioning Element**   | **Direction**                                                                                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Category                  | Shopify dropshipping and product-sourcing automation platform.                                                                                                                    |
| Target audience           | Shopify store owners, dropshipping beginners, growing merchants, product hunters and eCommerce operators.                                                                         |
| Primary value proposition | AeroDrop combines product discovery, one-click import, listing control, fulfillment visibility and real-time business insight in one merchant-friendly platform.                  |
| Differentiation direction | Beginner-friendly workflow, free entry plan, AliExpress-focused importing, AI-assisted paid features, operational dashboard, brand-first sourcing and scalable multi-store plans. |
| Brand enemy               | Repetitive copy-paste work, disconnected supplier tabs, manual product edits, uncertain pricing, scattered order updates and avoidable operational delay.                         |
| Brand idea                | Dropshipping operations made simpler.                                                                                                                                             |

### **Brand Personality, Voice & Tone**

| **Element**         | **Guideline**                                                                                                                                                      |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Brand personality   | Entrepreneurial, helpful, energetic, practical, modern and growth-oriented.                                                                                        |
| Brand voice         | A capable eCommerce partner that removes unnecessary complexity and guides merchants toward a clearer workflow.                                                    |
| Communication style | Use short, direct and benefit-led language. Show the operational problem, demonstrate the workflow and finish with one clear action.                               |
| Language guidance   | Use simple English. Keep familiar Shopify and dropshipping terms in English. Explain technical functions in merchant language.                                     |
| Do                  | Focus on time saved, fewer repetitive steps, listing quality, order clarity, shipping options, pricing visibility and scalable workflows.                          |
| Do not              | Do not guarantee profit, sales, winning products, delivery time or passive income. Avoid hype-heavy “get rich quick” messaging and unsupported performance claims. |

### **Voice in Practice - Before / After Examples**

The pairs below show generic dropshipping-app copy next to an
AeroDrop-voiced rewrite, to calibrate an AI writer or copywriter
quickly.

| **Generic (avoid)**                                  | **AeroDrop Voice (use)**                                                                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| “Make \$10,000/month dropshipping with zero effort!” | “Spend less time copy-pasting product data and more time building your store.”                                                  |
| “Our AI finds guaranteed winning products.”          | “Discover top-selling and trending products, curated from a catalog of over 1 million items.”                                   |
| “Fully automated - you never have to do anything.”   | “Automated shipping and fulfillment lets you focus on marketing and growth.”                                                    |
| “Ship anywhere in 2 days, guaranteed.”               | “Access suppliers offering faster global shipping options.” (qualify by supplier/route - never state a universal delivery time) |

A single text field labelled “Shopify Store Link” with the placeholder
format example “Ex: https://admin.shopify.com/store/xxxx”, paired with

Instructional copy: “When accessing the app page, click Install to

## **Screen: Find Products**


*Find Products - the AliExpress discovery and sourcing catalog.*

**Purpose:** The product-research engine of the platform - this is where

### **Controls**

- **Select Category -** dropdown defaulting to “All categories.”

- **Search products by title, AliExpress link, or image -** a single

### **Product Grid**

A responsive card grid, each card showing a product photo, a truncated
title, and a “Product Cost” price in US dollars (observed range roughly

entry point into the import workflow - selecting one is expected to move

</colgroup>

<p>The combination of title search, direct AliExpress link paste, and

## **Screen: Draft Products**


*Draft Products - Draft List tab, empty state.*

**Purpose:** The staging and editing workspace between “found on
AliExpress” and “live on the Shopify store.”

### **Tabs**

- **Draft List -** products imported from Find Products but not yet
  published; columns are Product and Connection Status.

- **In Progress List -** products actively being edited/prepared
  (titles, descriptions, images, variants, pricing) before publish.

- **Store Listings & Sourcing -** the bridge view connecting a prepared
  draft to its live Shopify listing and its AliExpress sourcing record.

- **Issues -** a dedicated queue for products that failed to import,
  publish or sync correctly, so problems don't get silently lost inside
  the main draft list.

A search field and the same Product / Connection Status columns are
consistent across the list-style tabs.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p><strong>Business logic note</strong></p>
<p>A dedicated “Issues” tab is a meaningful operational design choice -
it is the difference between a merchant discovering a broken import
themselves (after a lost sale) and AeroDrop surfacing the problem
proactively. This should be a marketing talking point (“nothing gets
silently lost”) as much as it is a UX feature.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## **Screen: My Products**


*My Products (labelled “Imported Products” on-screen) - empty state.*

**Purpose:** The system-of-record for everything currently
published/live on the connected Shopify store via AeroDrop.

### **Columns**

- Product - the published product name/thumbnail.

- Brand - the brand attribution attached to the listing.

- Variants - count or list of size/colour/style variants under the
  product.

- Last Modified Date - the most recent edit or sync timestamp.

A search field sits above the table for quickly locating a specific SKU
across a large catalog.

## **Screen: Orders**


*Orders - empty state.*

**Purpose:** The fulfillment control tower - every customer order from
the connected Shopify store, cross-referenced against its supplier
(“third party”) order.

### **Columns**

- Name - order identifier/number.

- Create Date - when the order was placed.

- Customer Name / Customer Email - buyer contact detail.

- Total - order value.

- Payment Status - e.g., paid/pending, synced from Shopify.

- Order Status - fulfillment stage on the Shopify side.

- Third Party Order - whether/how the order has been placed with the
  supplier (AliExpress).

- Third Party Order Tracking - the supplier-side tracking reference once
  dispatched.

- Actions - per-row operations (e.g., manually place/re-sync the
  supplier order).

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p><strong>Business logic note</strong></p>
<p>This table is the operational proof behind the website's “Automated
Shipping &amp; Fulfillment” and “Monitor Sales in Real Time” promises:
it is the single place a merchant reconciles “a customer paid me”
against “I have ordered and can track this from my supplier,” which is
precisely the manual spreadsheet work AeroDrop is positioned to
replace.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## **Screen: Pricing Rules**


*Pricing Rule - Basic and Standard rule builders.*

**Purpose:** The markup engine that converts a supplier's Product Cost
into the price shown on the merchant's own storefront, and optionally
into a “compared at” (strikethrough) price.

### **Basic Pricing Rule**

A single-formula rule: Product Cost \[operator: + or –\] \[amount\] =
Price. A toggle labelled “Set your compared at pricing rules” reveals an
identical second formula - Product Cost \[operator\] \[amount\] =
Compared at Price - letting a merchant show an inflated “original price”
next to the actual selling price for perceived-discount marketing. A
Save button commits the rule.

### **Standard Pricing Rule (Tiered)**

A cost-banded table: for each Starting Price–Ending Price range of the
supplier's Product Cost, the merchant sets an Operator Field, a markup
amount, and an optional Compared at Price with its own operator and
amount. Rows can be deleted (trash icon) and added, and a final “Rest of
the ranges” fallback rule catches any product cost outside the defined
bands so nothing is left unpriced.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p><strong>Business logic note</strong></p>
<p>The tiered model exists because flat markups do not work across a
wide cost range: a fixed +$10 markup is a healthy margin on a $5 item
and an unsellable price on a $2 item, while a flat percentage can
under-price expensive items relative to perceived value. Standard
Pricing Rule is the more sophisticated, retention-relevant feature and
deserves more prominence in onboarding and paid-plan messaging than it
currently receives on the marketing site.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## **Screen: Order Settings**


*Order Settings - automated supplier order placement.*

**Purpose:** Controls whether customer orders are forwarded to
AliExpress automatically.

**On-screen copy:** “Our system includes an Automated Supplier Order
Placement feature. When a client completes an order on your store, the
system instantly and automatically sends that order to AliExpress for
fulfillment. This eliminates the need for manual processing, reduces
errors, and ensures faster delivery. By automating the entire workflow,
you save time and streamline your dropshipping operations, allowing you
to focus on business growth instead of routine tasks.”

The screen shows a connected supplier account (“Ali Express949”) with a
per-account on/off toggle - captured here in the off position, meaning
automatic order placement is an opt-in control the merchant switches on
deliberately rather than a forced default.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p><strong>Business logic note</strong></p>
<p>Defaulting this to off is a sound trust decision - it means a
merchant's first orders will not be auto-forwarded to a supplier until
they have explicitly reviewed and enabled the behaviour, reducing the

# **06 - Merchant Onboarding Journey (Unified User Guide)**

This is a single, corrected step-by-step sequence that reconciles the
website's 4-step explainer, the in-app Connect Store screen, and the
full sidebar navigation into one definitive Standard Operating
Procedure. It is written so it can be dropped directly into a Help
Center article, a welcome email series, or an AI support-bot's answer
for “How do I get started with AeroDrop?”

**Step 1 - Create an AeroDrop account.** Sign up in seconds to access
the full dropshipping toolset, resources and support. No credit card
required to begin on the Free plan.

**Step 2 - Connect a Shopify store.** From the Connect Store screen,
paste the Shopify store link (format:
https://admin.shopify.com/store/xxxx) and select Authorize to grant
AeroDrop access via Shopify's standard app-authorization flow.

**Step 3 - Install the AeroDrop app on Shopify.** From the Shopify App
Store listing, click Install to enable one-click product listing and
automatic order fulfillment for the connected store.

**Step 4 - Browse or search for products.** Use Find Products to browse
by category, use the quick filters (Hot Selling, Special Deals, New
Products, Trending), or search directly by title, AliExpress link, or
product image.

**Step 5 - Move selected products into Draft Products.** Selected items
land in the Draft List, ready for review and editing before they go
live.

**Step 6 - Edit and prepare each listing.** Refine titles, descriptions,
images, variants and category inside Draft Products (In Progress List)
until the listing is ready for the storefront.

**Step 7 - Set a pricing rule.** Configure a Basic pricing rule (single
markup formula) or a Standard pricing rule (tiered, cost-banded markups)
in Pricing Rules so every imported product is priced automatically and
consistently.

**Step 8 - Publish to the Shopify store.** Send the prepared draft live;
it then appears in My Products as a published, tracked SKU with its
brand and variant detail.

**Step 9 - Decide on automated order placement.** In Order Settings,
choose whether customer orders should be sent to AliExpress
automatically the moment a sale completes, or handled manually.

**Step 10 - Market the store and receive orders.** Drive traffic and
sales through the merchant's own marketing efforts; incoming orders
populate the Orders screen with payment status, order status and
supplier tracking.

**Step 11 - Fulfill and track.** Monitor each order's Third Party Order
status and tracking reference until delivery; use the Issues tab in
Draft Products and Support Ticket for anything that needs
troubleshooting.

**Step 12 - Review performance and reinvest.** Use the Dashboard's
Imported Products, Orders and Total Sales metrics over a chosen date
range to evaluate what's working, then return to Find Products to source
the next batch of winners.

### **First-Week Success Checklist (for onboarding emails / in-app checklist)**

- Shopify store connected and authorized.

- AeroDrop app installed from the Shopify App Store.

- At least one pricing rule configured (Basic or Standard).

- First product imported, edited and published.

- Order Settings reviewed and a deliberate choice made on automatic
  supplier ordering.

- First order received and successfully tracked through to the supplier.

  features from upcoming improvements.

  12-step SOP in Section 06 so the site never under-promises the setup
  effort.

# **14 - Content System & Funnel Mapping**

| **Funnel Stage** | **Message**                                                                  | **Content Format**                          | **CTA**              |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| Awareness        | Manual dropshipping takes longer than merchants expect.                      | Problem-led reels, blogs, founder posts     | Explore AeroDrop     |
| Consideration    | Show product discovery, import, editing and fulfillment workflow.            | Tutorials, carousels, comparisons, webinars | Install Free         |
| Conversion       | Remove pricing, capability and onboarding objections.                        | App Store assets, demo clips, FAQs, email   | Connect Store        |
| Activation       | Guide the merchant to first imported and published product.                  | Checklist, in-app guide, email sequence     | Import First Product |
| Retention        | Help merchants use price updates, dashboard and order workflow consistently. | Tips, reports, feature education            | Use Weekly           |
| Expansion        | Show value of more product imports, unlimited orders and additional stores.  | Usage-based prompts, success stories        | Upgrade Plan         |

# **15 - SWOT Analysis**

A working-level SWOT built from what is directly observable across the
site, app and listing today - useful as a standing reference for
planning and for an AI assistant asked to reason about AeroDrop's
competitive position.

### **Strengths**

- A genuinely complete, connected workflow - discovery, import, editing,
  pricing rules, automated supplier ordering and a live dashboard -
  rather than a single-feature tool.

- A generous, real Free plan (500 products, 200 orders/month, one store)
  that lets merchants prove value before paying.

- A two-tier pricing engine (Basic and Standard/tiered) that is more
  sophisticated than flat-markup pricing offered by many entry-level
  competitors.

- Dedicated Issues tracking inside Draft Products, reducing silent
  failures.

- Dual support channels - instant WhatsApp chat plus a formal ticket
  system.

- Clear, transparent, immediately-effective plan upgrade/downgrade
  policy.

### **Weaknesses**

- Zero public reviews on the Shopify App Store at time of audit, versus
  55–325 reviews on direct neighboring competitors.

- Pricing inconsistency between the in-app Pricing Plan screen and other
  AeroApps-associated pricing references.

- The homepage's 4-step onboarding explainer ends on a resource (Help
  Center) rather than the actual final action (publish/go live).

- Limited visible video/tutorial content for a workflow-heavy product
  that benefits strongly from visual demonstration.

- Stale footer copyright year, a small but visible signal of site
  maintenance recency.

### **Opportunities**

- Convert the existing review-gated 30-day Premium offer into the
  primary lever for closing the reviews gap against competitors.

- Lean into the Dhaka, Bangladesh / South Asian operating base to own
  localized, first-time-entrepreneur onboarding content that larger,
  US/EU-headquartered competitors under-serve.

- Publish direct comparison content against the five strongest named
  competitors while the category is still actively searched.

- Build a verified customer-proof pipeline from the ten reference
  merchants already on file.

- Use the Standard (tiered) Pricing Rule as a distinct, demonstrable
  differentiator in comparison and consideration-stage content.

### **Threats**

- A crowded competitive set (at least ten established alternatives)
  where switching cost for a merchant is low.

- AliExpress-dependency risk - single-supplier integration until
  additional suppliers are added to the Select Supplier dropdown.

- Generic “get rich quick” dropshipping messaging saturating paid and
  organic channels, making an honest, time-saving-focused brand voice
  harder to stand out with unless proof-led content is prioritized.

- Shipping-time expectations remain a persistent category-wide trust
  risk that any absolute claim would worsen - reinforcing the guardrails
  in Section 16.

# **16 - Claims & Compliance Guardrails**

- Do not promise guaranteed profit, winning products, passive income or
  a specific sales result.

- Do not present 2–7 day shipping as universal; qualify it by supplier,
  product, destination and shipping method.

- Do not publish review counts or star ratings until the AeroApps page
  and Shopify App Store listing are reconciled.

- Do not promote Chrome extension, full automatic supplier ordering,
  custom packaging or subscription boxes as universally available
  without current product confirmation.

- Use “helps reduce manual work” rather than “zero work” or “fully
  passive.”

- Ensure product sourcing, shipping, returns, taxes and
  consumer-protection responsibilities are clear to the merchant.

- Do not state a specific pricing figure externally until the Section 07
  pricing discrepancy is resolved with the product/finance team.

- Do not describe empty-state dashboard screens (as captured in this
  demo-account audit) as showing live performance data in any external
  material.

# **18 - Appendix**

### **A. Glossary of Terms**

- **AliExpress -** the primary supplier marketplace AeroDrop currently
  sources products from.

- **Compared at Price -** an inflated reference price shown alongside
  the actual selling price, typically displayed with a strikethrough to
  signal a discount.

- **Draft product -** a product imported from a supplier but not yet
  published to the merchant's live Shopify storefront.

- **Dropshipping -** a retail model where the merchant sells a product
  without holding inventory; the supplier ships directly to the end
  customer once an order is placed.

- **Fulfillment -** the process of getting a purchased product from the
  supplier to the customer, including order placement, shipping and
  tracking.

- **Markup / pricing rule -** the formula that converts a supplier's
  product cost into the merchant's own selling price.

- **Product cost -** the price the merchant pays the supplier for a unit
  of product, before markup.

- **SKU -** stock-keeping unit; a unique identifier for a specific
  product or product variant.

- **Third-party order -** AeroDrop's term for the corresponding order
  placed with the supplier (AliExpress) once a customer buys on the
  merchant's storefront.

- **Variant -** a specific version of a product (e.g., a size or colour
  option) tracked separately within a single product listing.

**Business Problems and AeroRank Response**

| **Problem**                  | **Impact**                                                                   | **AeroRank Response**                                                    |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Manual content writing**   | Products launch with weak or incomplete descriptions.                        | Generate structured, search-intent-led product and collection content.   |
| **Missing metadata**         | Search snippets are weak, incomplete or inconsistent.                        | Create and improve meta titles and descriptions individually or in bulk. |
| **Low SEO clarity**          | Merchants do not know which problems matter first.                           | Use audit scores, issue categories and guided actions.                   |
| **Large catalogue effort**   | Page-by-page updates consume time and become inconsistent.                   | Apply templates, bulk actions and automation.                            |
| **Image SEO gaps**           | Missing alt text and large image files reduce accessibility and performance. | Use image alt-text and optimization workflows as released.               |
| **Broken links**             | Visitors and search engines reach unavailable pages.                         | Identify and redirect broken links as released.                          |
| **Thin / duplicate content** | Pages provide limited differentiation or search relevance.                   | Use AI rewrite and search-intent suggestions.                            |
| **Technical SEO complexity** | Structured data, schema and performance issues feel difficult.               | Translate technical issues into merchant-friendly actions.               |

**Merchant Activation Journey**

- Install: open the Shopify App Store listing and add Aero SEO Rank AI
  > to the selected store.

- Enable: review permissions, activate the app and select relevant
  > optimization features.

- Audit: scan the store and review the SEO score, issue categories and
  > priority pages.

- Optimize: generate or improve product titles, descriptions, keywords
  > and metadata.

- Resolve: address content, metadata, image and broken-link issues
  > according to released features.

- Review: compare the existing and proposed content before publishing
  > changes.

- Automate: apply bulk and scheduled workflows for large catalogues and
  > new products.

- Measure: review SEO scores, issue reduction, activation, content
  > coverage and merchant outcomes.

# **01. Product Identity, Architecture & Naming Rules**

## **1.1 What Managerium ERP is**

**Managerium ERP** is AKIJ iBOS's comprehensive, all-industry enterprise
resource planning platform. It is the complete version of Managerium:
one connected system covering procurement, sales, export sales, point of
sale, accounts and finance, inventory and warehouse, payroll and HR,
quality control, fixed assets, production, approvals and governance,
configuration, after-sales service, and route-to-market field execution.

Its central idea is to replace scattered data, disconnected tools,
manual follow-up and delayed reporting with a single operating model
that gives decision-makers visibility, accuracy, control, speed and the
ability to scale without losing grip on the business.

The live product has **fifteen top-level modules** and several hundred
individual features. It is not a POS with add-ons and it is not an
accounting package with extras. It is a full ERP that also happens to
contain a strong retail and field-sales layer.

# **02. Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)**

Managerium ERP is best suited to growing organisations that have
outgrown spreadsheets, manual reporting and disconnected software, and
now need reliable control across finance, sales, purchase, inventory,
production, payroll and outlet or field operations.

## **2.1 ICP questions**

| **Question**                            | **Answer**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Who are they?**                       | Business owners and Managing Directors, CEOs, COOs and Operations Heads, CFOs and Accounts Heads, Retail Heads, Distribution and Sales Heads, Factory and Production Heads, IT Heads and CIOs, and Business Unit Heads inside multi-entity groups. Organisation types: trading houses, manufacturers, distributors, service companies, retailers and multi-outlet chains, and group or multi-entity businesses. |
| **What do they currently think?**       | That the current setup is "manageable". Excel plus a POS plus an accounting package plus a few experienced employees plus phone calls. They believe ERP is expensive, complex, disruptive, and that their team will struggle to adopt it. Many have been quoted by a global ERP vendor and found the number unrealistic.                                                                                        |
| **What problem do they face?**          | Scattered data with no single source of truth. Stock that does not match between counter, warehouse and accounts. Reports that arrive days late. Purchases and expenses approved without visibility. Finance re-entering operational data by hand. No ability to compare branch or outlet performance quickly. Growth that depends on a small number of irreplaceable people.                                   |
| **What do we want them to think?**      | That Managerium is not "more software" - it is one connected operating system for the whole business, built and supported locally, that turns follow-up-based management into report-and-dashboard-based management, and turns person-dependent execution into defined process.                                                                                                                                 |
| **What action do we want?**             | Book a demo, schedule a strategy call, or accept a process assessment covering purchase, stock, finance and reporting gaps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **What proof will convince them?**      | A live dashboard answering a question they currently have to phone three people to answer. Named customers in their own industry. A visible approval trail. An implementation method they can see. Financial ratio analysis and procurement cycle-time analytics they did not know software could give them.                                                                                                    |
| **What tone should we use?**            | Practical, business-first, problem-led, confidence-building. Speak to owners, CFOs, COOs and Retail or Distribution Heads in operational language, not technical language. Explain the consequence before the feature.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Which channels will influence them?** | Google Search for high-intent ERP, POS, inventory and manufacturing software queries. LinkedIn for CXO authority. Facebook and YouTube for pain-led education and testimonials. Webinars and monthly demo days. Direct sales meetings and sales decks. Industry events. Referrals from existing AKIJ iBOS customers.                                                                                            |

| **Trading & Distribution**      | Purchase, multi-warehouse stock, sales, receivables, route and territory visibility, reporting.                                 | Owner/MD, Sales Head, Distribution Head, CFO      | Purchase + Inventory + Sales + RTM            |
| **Retail & Multi-Outlet**       | POS, pricing, discounts, returns, stock transfer, accounting, loyalty, payroll and outlet visibility.                           | Owner, Retail Head, COO, CFO, IT Head             | POS + Inventory + Account                     |
| **Service Business**            | Billing, customer management, service requests, approvals, payroll, expenses and management reporting.                          | Owner, CEO, CFO, Operations Head                  | POST CRM + Account + Payroll                  |
| **Group / Multi-Entity**        | Consolidated reporting, user permissions, branch control, approval hierarchy, scalability.                                      | Group MD, CFO, CIO/IT Head, Business Unit Heads   | Multilayer Approval + Account + Configuration |
| **Exporter / Import-dependent** | Foreign purchase orders, shipment and charge conditions, LC management, export LC, proforma invoicing, export sales scheduling. | MD, CFO, Commercial Head, Merchandising Head      | Export Sales + LC Management + Purchase       |

*The exporter segment is not currently addressed anywhere in Managerium
marketing, despite the product having a complete export and
trade-finance capability. See Section 05.4.*

## **2.3 Buying triggers**

- Opening new outlets, warehouses, branches or production units.

- Repeated stock mismatch, leakage, shrinkage or reconciliation problems
  between counter, warehouse and accounts.

- Management wanting live dashboards instead of end-of-day or weekly
  manual reporting.

- Existing POS, accounting, HR or inventory tools that cannot talk to
  each other.

- Audit pressure, VAT or NBR compliance requirements, or a need for
  demonstrable process accountability.

- Growth becoming dependent on a small number of experienced employees.

- An owner who can no longer understand the business without asking
  several people for updates.

- A failed or stalled implementation with another vendor.

- A new CFO, COO or IT Head arriving with a mandate to systematise.

- Preparing for investment, acquisition or group consolidation, where
  clean books and audit trails become mandatory.

## **2.4 Buyer mindset before contact**

A typical prospect is not sitting at zero. They usually already own
something: a POS, a Tally-style accounting file, a biometric attendance
device, an Excel stock register. Their pain is not the absence of
software. Their pain is that none of it connects, and that the
connecting is being done by human beings under time pressure.

This matters for messaging. Managerium should almost never open with
"you need software". It should open with the specific consequence of
disconnection - the stock that does not match, the report that comes too
late, the discount nobody authorised, the supplier payment nobody
tracked.

## **2.5 Disqualifiers - when Managerium ERP is not the right sell**

| **Situation**                                                                    | **What to do instead**                                                                           |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Single small retail outlet, one counter, no back office**                      | Sell Managerium Retail ERP, not the full ERP. Do not oversize the deal.                          |
| **Hospital, clinic or multi-specialty healthcare organisation**                  | Sell Managerium Health.                                                                          |
| **Business that only needs HR and payroll**                                      | Sell PeopleDesk. See Section 06.7 for the boundary rule.                                         |
| **Business that only needs VAT management**                                      | Sell PrimeVAT.                                                                                   |
| **Organisation with no process ownership and no willingness to change workflow** | ERP will fail. Qualify hard on leadership ownership at discovery, not after signature.           |
| **Buyer looking purely for the cheapest possible licence**                       | Compete on outcome, not price. If the conversation stays on price alone, this is not an ICP fit. |

|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| **CFO / Accounts Head**       | Transaction accuracy, AR/AP, reconciliation, audit readiness, closing speed. | Finance should receive structured operational data instead of chasing it.                | Financial Ratio Analysis, bank reconciliation, budget vs actual, journal approvals.         |

| **Retail Head**               | POS speed, branch stock, pricing, returns, discounts, customer insight.      | From counter to management dashboard, activity stays connected.                          | POS counter flow, outlet-wise sales, discount authorisation.                                |
| **Distribution / Sales Head** | Market execution, distributor stock, field team, secondary sales.            | See what happens after products reach distributors and keep field execution accountable. | RTM dashboard, IMS and strike rate, outlet coverage map.                                    |
| **IT Head / CIO**             | Security, scalability, configurability, supportability, data control.        | A modern, modular ERP with permission groups, audit logs and implementation support.     | Permission groups, audit log, system risk controls, identity & security, API configuration. |
| **Factory / Production Head** | Yield, wastage, machine utilisation, material availability.                  | Every unit produced and every material consumed, tracked the moment it happens.          | BOM with wastage, work centre, production order approval chain.                             |

# **03. Brand Guideline**

## **3.1 Brand foundation**

| **Element**         | **Definition**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Brand purpose**   | Simplify and integrate core business operations through a smart, reliable ERP that helps organisations gain control, work faster and make better decisions.                                                                                             |
| **Mission**         | Deliver a scalable, cloud-based ERP connecting procurement, sales, inventory, finance, HR, payroll, assets, production, POS, CRM, mobile access, VAT/NBR support, business intelligence and real-time reporting - backed by implementation and support. |
| **Vision**          | Become the trusted business operating system for growing organisations by making complex operations simple, connected and future-ready.                                                                                                                 |
| **Core values**     | Simplicity. Reliability. Integration. Innovation. Practical excellence. Data clarity. Client commitment. Scalability. Long-term value creation.                                                                                                         |
| **Core brand idea** | **Simple operations. Connected control. Future-ready business.**                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Key message**     | **One connected ERP for complete business control.**                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Brand promise**   | Simpler, smarter, more controlled and more scalable operations through one reliable platform and consistent support.                                                                                                                                    |
| **Brand archetype** | Sage + Creator. Knowledgeable, practical, solution-building, business-oriented.                                                                                                                                                                         |

## **3.2 Brand personality and voice**

**Personality:** intelligent, dependable, clear, practical, modern,
confident, solution-driven.

**Communication style:** clear, business-first, educational, supportive
and confident. The recommended narrative is always the same shape -
explain the business pain, give the operational context, show the
connected response, close on measurable value.

### **Do**

- Focus on clarity, control, speed, integration, data visibility and
  business outcomes.

- Lead with a specific operational situation the reader recognises.

- Use simple business English. In Bangla-primary content, use natural
  Bangla with familiar software and business terms left in English.

- Use short sentences and active voice.

- Name the module or workflow when it makes the claim more credible.

### **Do not**

- Overpromise, especially on automation, alerts and efficiency
  percentages.

- Use slang-heavy corporate language or buzzword stacking.

- Create cluttered copy where three claims compete in one headline.

- Rely only on fear. Loss framing is allowed, but it must resolve into a
  concrete capability.

- Publish inconsistent claims across pages, decks and ads.

- Use generic "smarter / faster / control" language unless it is tied to
  a specific operation.

| **Dark emphasis**        | Deep Navy       | \#13264D | Headers, dark backgrounds, high-contrast type, app chrome.                       |
| **CTA accent**           | Digital Red     | \#FD0000 | Calls to action and single points of emphasis only. Never as a background field. |
| **Primary background**   | White           | \#FFFFFF | Dominant background. Whitespace is part of the identity.                         |
| **Neutral**              | Light Grey      | \#E0E0E0 | Dividers, secondary surfaces, disabled states.                                   |

**Suggested ratio:** approximately 60% white, 30% Managerium Blue or
Deep Navy, 10% Digital Red. The red is a scalpel, not a brush.

## <img src="media/image2.png" style="width:3.40719in;height:0.58603in" />**3.5 Logo**

*Managerium primary lockup - Deep Navy mark with Digital Red accent,
Managerium Blue wordmark.*

- The mark is a rounded-square navy tile carrying a stylised "M" with a
  red accent. The wordmark is set in heavy weight, all capitals.

- Preserve clear space of at least the height of the mark on all sides.

- Do not recolour the mark, stretch the lockup, add effects, or place
  the navy mark on a navy field without sufficient contrast.

- On dark backgrounds use the reversed lockup. On product screenshots
  the logo already appears in the interface header - do not add a second
  logo on top.

## **3.6 Imagery**

- Professional offices, factories, warehouses, retail outlets, pharmacy
  counters and meeting rooms.

- Real decision-makers and teams using real workflows, not stock-photo
  gestures.

- Dashboard cards, process maps, workflow lines and reporting graphics
  where they clarify the message.

- Scenario-first storytelling. If the copy is about fragmented data,
  show two people comparing two conflicting reports - not floating
  icons.

- Screen UI shown naturally, at a believable scale. Never as a giant
  decorative hologram.

## **3.7 Layout**

Strong white space and a clear F or Z reading hierarchy: **headline →
product or visual → benefit → CTA**. One idea per block. Do not stack
three competing claims in a single band.

Social formats: 1:1 and 4:5 for feed, 9:16 for Reels and Stories, 16:9
for video.

## **3.9 Local vs international communication**

The brand runs two communication contexts. **Local** content uses
natural Bangla-English business language, the locked Bangla CTA, and
Bangladesh-specific proof. **International** content uses cleaner
English, is less locally anchored, and leads on capability and standards
rather than local familiarity.

Formal logo and company-endorsement rules differ by market and should be
confirmed before any international campaign runs.

# **05. Product Details - Positioning, Value Pillars & Differentiation**

## **5.1 Positioning statement**

<table>

<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>Managerium ERP positioning</strong></p>
<p>For growing Bangladeshi organisations that have outgrown spreadsheets
and disconnected tools, <strong>Managerium ERP is one connected business
operating system</strong> that brings procurement, sales, inventory,
finance, production, payroll, retail counters, field distribution and
governance into a single platform - with local implementation, local
support and local compliance understanding.</p>
<p>Unlike global ERP platforms, it is affordable and adaptable to how
Bangladeshi businesses actually operate. Unlike local POS and accounting
tools, it does not stop at the counter or the ledger.</p></th>

## **5.2 Core value pillars**

| **Pillar**      | **Business meaning**                                                                                                               | **What proves it in the product**                                                                                                       |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Visibility**  | Dashboards, branch and outlet views, module reports and management insight reduce dependence on manual follow-up.                  | Ten module dashboards, 360° leaderboard, layer-wise drilldown, coverage days, financial ratio analysis.                                 |
| **Accuracy**    | Structured transactions, connected records and instant stock updates reduce mismatch and repeated manual entry.                    | Transaction-linked inventory, stock adjustment with audit, item stock conversion, bank reconciliation.                                  |
| **Control**     | Approvals, permissions, audit trails and accountable actions.                                                                      | ~50 approval types across nine groups, Multilayer Approval, permission groups, audit log, backdate configuration, system risk controls. |
| **Speed**       | Faster billing, reporting, approvals, reconciliation and decision-making.                                                          | POS counter flow, one-click financial reports, mobile approvals, real-time dashboards.                                                  |
| **Scalability** | Growth from a single operation to multi-outlet, multi-warehouse, multi-plant and multi-entity structures through modular adoption. | Business Unit / Office / Branch / Warehouse entities, multi-office payroll, multi-plant production, consolidated financials.            |
| **Support**     | Guided implementation, training and continuing improvement as part of the offer.                                                   | Seven-stage implementation method, role-based training, documented user manuals, release notes in-product.                              |

## **5.3 Differentiation themes**

- **One connected platform** across finance, sales, purchase, export,
  inventory, production, payroll, fixed assets, POS, quality, service
  and field distribution.

- **Bangladesh-ready** implementation, local process understanding, VAT
  and NBR context, and local support proximity.

- **Retail depth inside an ERP** - outlet visibility, pricing, offers,
  loyalty, payroll, accounting and counter operations, not bolted on.

- **Field distribution depth inside an ERP** - a full RTM
  secondary-sales layer with FMCG-grade KPIs, which almost no local ERP
  carries.

- **Governance depth** - around fifty distinct approval types with live
  pending counts, plus multilayer approval chains.

- **Analytical depth beyond reporting** - procurement cycle time by
  stage, supplier classification bands, inventory coverage days,
  inventory turnover ratio, and a standard-versus-actual financial ratio
  table.

- **Business-control language for owners and CXOs**, rather than
  feature-only technical communication.

## **5.4 Strong capabilities that are currently unsold**

This section exists because the gap between what Managerium does and
what Managerium says is large. Each item below is present and visible in
the live product but appears nowhere in current marketing.

### **A. Export and trade finance**

The product contains a complete export and import trade-finance
capability: an **Export Sales** module (Proforma Invoice, Export Sales
Order, Shipment Schedule, Sales Delivery, Collection, LC Fees Config),
**LC Management** and **Export LC Management** in Accounts, **LC
Margin**, **Foreign Purchase Orders** with shipment creation and charge
conditions, **Intending Purchase**, and four dedicated export approvals
(Export Sales Order, Export Sales Schedule, Export Sales LC Fees,
Proforma Invoice).

Not one word of this appears on any landing page or the ERP product
page. For RMG exporters, trading houses, importers and export-oriented
manufacturers, this is the single most compelling reason to choose
Managerium over a domestic POS-plus-accounting stack. **This is the
largest identified positioning opportunity in the product.**

### **B. Manufacturing sub-vertical depth**

The Manufacturing landing page describes the capability as "Bill of
Materials and Work Center tracking". The live Production module
contains: Work Center, Bill of Material, Equipment, **Dairy
Production**, **Formulation Setup**, **Material Requirement**,
Production Order, **Contract Manufacturing**, Production Entry,
**Sample**, **Sample Tech Pack**, **Costing** and Production Report -
plus dedicated approvals for Sample Design, Merchandiser Costing and
Dairy Production.

That combination supports at least three distinct manufacturing
sub-verticals: **process and food / dairy** (formulation, dairy
production, chilling-centre and tanker warehouses), **RMG and apparel**
(sample, tech pack, merchandiser costing), and **discrete
manufacturing** (work centres such as blow moulding, polishing, bottle
make). None of it is marketed.

### **C. Financial ratio analysis**

The Account Dashboard ships a built-in **Financial Ratio Analysis**
table with standard ratio versus actual ratio benchmarking across
liquidity ratios, profitability ratios and activity or
management-efficiency ratios. This is a CFO-grade capability that very
few competitors in this market advertise, and it is invisible in current
marketing.

### **D. Procurement analytics**

The Purchase Dashboard shows **average procurement cycle time broken
into five stages** - Order Placement, Confirmation, Delivery, Invoicing,
Payment - each with a day count, plus an **on-time payment rate** and
**supplier classification into Short, Medium and Long cycle bands**.
This is procurement performance management, not purchase recording. It
is not marketed.

### **E. Inventory science**

The Inventory Dashboard shows **Coverage Days** (daily consumption
against stock availability per item), **Inventory Turnover Ratio**,
**Item Moving Frequency** and valuation split by MRO, Asset, Raw and
Finished Goods. This is the honest and defensible version of the
stock-out story - consumption-based coverage analysis rather than an
alert claim.

### **F. Quality management**

**QC Management** with QC Parameter Assign and Quality Control is a live
module. It appears in no document and no marketing material. For
manufacturing and food processing buyers, quality parameters are
frequently a hard requirement.

### **G. After-sales service management**

**POST CRM** contains Complaint Management, Service Request, Service
Agreement and Service Report. This is an after-sales service desk, not a
sales CRM. For any business selling equipment, appliances, machinery or
serviced products, this closes the loop from sale to warranty to service
contract. Unmarketed.

### **H. Fuel and forecourt retail**

The POS module contains a **Fuel Price Update** function alongside Item
Selling Price Update. That is a purpose-built capability for fuel
stations and forecourt retail - a vertical that appears nowhere in the
industry list.

### **I. Product governance signals**

The interface carries a **Release Note** section, a global "Go to page"
search, **voice input**, a **QR scanner**, a favourites system and
in-app chat. Release notes in particular are a maturity signal worth
using in enterprise sales, where buyers ask how the product evolves and
how changes are communicated.

## **6.1 Purchase**

End-to-end procurement, from an internal requisition through supplier
quotation comparison, purchase order, receiving, return and payment -
with dedicated analytics on top.

| **Feature**                       | **What it does**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Purchase Dashboard**            | Procurement analytics: type-wise purchase, warehouse-wise purchase, pending invoices and pending receipts, on-time payment rate, average procurement cycle time by stage, purchase expenditure trend, supplier classification, top 10 suppliers and top 10 items.                                                               |
| **Purchase Requisition**          | Internal request for goods or services. Requisition type can be Employee, Department or Project. Captures project, office, warehouse, expected date, item, quantity, rate, description, budget total and remarks.                                                                                                               |
| **Request For Quotation (RFQ)**   | Formal quotation request issued to suppliers or vendors against a requisition.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Quotation Entry**               | Records supplier responses to an RFQ with full quotation details.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Comparative Statement**         | Side-by-side comparison of received quotations, with the ability to push the winning quotation directly into a Purchase Order.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Advance Comparative Statement** | Extended comparison capability beyond the standard comparative statement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Purchase Order**                | Four order types: **Local Purchase**, **Foreign Purchase** (with currency details, shipping details, shipment creation and charge conditions), **Intending Purchase**, and configurable **Purchase Method**. Captures create-from source, date details, supplier, shipping, currency, item list, order summary and order total. |
| **Purchase Receive**              | Goods receipt. Supports **Direct Receive** and **PO-wise Receive**, with a view of received POs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Purchase Return**               | Returns to supplier, PO-wise or direct, full or partial, with a return list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Purchase Payment**              | Supplier payment recording against invoices and purchase orders.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Purchase Analytics**            | Analytical views over purchase activity.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Purchase Report**               | Standard purchase reporting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |


*Purchase Dashboard - type-wise and warehouse-wise purchase, pending
list, on-time payment rate, five-stage procurement cycle time,
expenditure trend, supplier classification bands, top suppliers and top
items.*

#### **Item type taxonomy visible in the product**

Asset · Asset Item · Finished Goods · Finished/Trading Goods ·
Finished/Trading Material · Maintenance, Repair and Operating Supplies
(MRO) · Marketing and Communication Material · Packaging Material ·
Production Tools and Resources · Raw Material · Semi Finished Goods ·
Service

*This taxonomy is useful in sales conversations because it demonstrates
that the system distinguishes trading stock from production input from
consumable from capital item - a distinction most POS-derived systems do
not make.*

A full retail counter system running on a Central Server plus counter
architecture, with online and offline sale synchronisation. Documented
separately in the Managerium POS System User Manual.

### **POS module features in the web portal**

| **Feature**                   | **What it does**                                                                                   |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **POS Sales**                 | Sales transactions from the POS module in the web application.                                     |
| **Item Selling Price Update** | Bulk or individual selling price updates pushed to counters.                                       |
| **Fuel Price Update**         | Dedicated fuel price update capability - supports fuel station and forecourt retail.               |
| **Special Discount**          | Special discount definitions beyond standard product discounts.                                    |
| **Discount & Offer**          | Discount and offer management.                                                                     |
| **Point Redemption**          | Loyalty point redemption rules and processing, with its own approval type (Point Redeem Approval). |
| **Return Exchange Rules**     | Rule set governing what can be returned or exchanged, under what conditions.                       |
| **POS Counter**               | Counter definition and management, including multi-counter operation.                              |
| **Negative Sales Setup**      | Configuration controlling whether and how negative stock sales are permitted.                      |
| **Vat Discount**              | VAT discount handling at the counter.                                                              |
| **Setup**                     | General POS setup and sales setup options.                                                         |
| **Data Log**                  | Data log of counter activity.                                                                      |
| **Price Tag**                 | Price tag generation and management.                                                               |
| **Reports**                   | POS reporting.                                                                                     |
| **MIS Report**                | Management information reporting from POS data.                                                    |
| **Central Sales Report**      | Consolidated sales reporting across counters and outlets.                                          |

### **POS counter workflow (from the POS user manual)**

| **Stage**                           | **What happens**                                                                                |
|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Starting the POS**                | Counter application launch and login. Web-based; requires browser and connection to the domain. |
| **Counter setup with Open Session** | Session opened against a defined counter before transactions can begin.                         |
| **Counter screen functionality**    | Main screen, Invoice page, About, Change Password.                                              |
| **Customer Management**             | Customer identification and creation at the counter.                                            |
| **Item Management**                 | Item search, selection and quantity handling, with barcode support.                             |
| **Reset All**                       | Clearing the current transaction from the screen.                                               |
| **Discount Management**             | Applying discounts under the configured rules and authorisation.                                |
| **Payment Management**              | Payment capture, including multiple payment methods.                                            |
| **Invoice Management**              | Invoice generation, printing and handling.                                                      |
| **Lock Session**                    | Session locking for cashier changeover and security.                                            |

### **POS central-server setup and reporting**

Configuration: Employee, Partner (Customer), Wallet Setup. Setup:
Selling Price Update, Point Offer, Point Redemption, Message Setup,
Product Discount, Special Discount, Sales Setup, Return Exchange, POS
Sales (Web). Reports: Inventory Report, POS Sales Report, Discount
Report, VAT Report, Data Log Report. Plus a **POS Dashboard** with
Sales, Inventory, Accounts and Customer sections.

Hardware components described: screen terminal, barcode scanner, card
processor machine, receipt printer, and records-keeping software. The
POS integration synchronises online and offline stores through a single
platform for payments, purchase tracking, customer data and invoicing.
