# **08. Approvals, Permissions & Governance Layer**

This is the strongest single control story in the product and it is
currently absent from all marketing. Managerium ships roughly **fifty
distinct approval types across nine functional groups**, each with a
live pending count, plus a separate Multilayer Approval module for
multi-level approval chains.


*The Approval dashboard - nine approval groups, each approval type
showing a live pending count.*

## **8.1 Full approval taxonomy**

| **Group**                  | **Approval types**                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Purchase Approval**      | Purchase Order · Purchase Bill · RFQ · Purchase Return · Purchase Requisition · Quotation Entry · Shipment · Purchase Clear Invoice                                                                                             |
| **Sales Approval**         | Sales Order · Sales Quotation · Sales Return · Sales Collection & Bill · Point Redeem · Schedule Delivery · Credit Limit · Clear Invoice · Export Sales Order · Proforma Invoice · Export Sales Schedule · Export Sales LC Fees |
| **Account Approval**       | Expense/Advance · Fund Transfer · Budget · Journal Voucher · Financial Budget · GL Merge · Chart Of Account                                                                                                                     |
| **HR Approval**            | Attendance Register · Employee Leave · Employee Movement · Employee Attendance · Employee Over Time · Salary Sheet · Bonus · Employee Increment · Service · Salary Advice · Bonus Advice · Separation                           |
| **Inventory Approval**     | Stock Adjustment · Inventory Requisition · Inventory Item Conversion · Transfer Request · Transfer Return                                                                                                                       |
| **Asset Approval**         | Asset Revaluation                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Production Approval**    | Production Order · Sample Design · Merchandiser Costing · Dairy Production · Production Entry                                                                                                                                   |
| **Configuration Approval** | Item Approval                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **RTM Approval**           | RTM Asset Requisition · Outlet Setup · Monthly Visit Plan                                                                                                                                                                       |

## **8.2 Multilayer Approval**

A separate top-level module sitting above Approval in the navigation. It
supports multi-level approval chains where a transaction must pass
through more than one authoriser before it takes effect. The RTM Damage
Control workflow explicitly uses a multi-level approval protocol; the
Production Order flow uses a three-step chain.

## **8.3 Permissions, audit and risk controls**

| **Control**                    | **What it does**                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Permission Group**           | Role-based access control determining which users can see and do what.                                                               |
| **User Group**                 | Grouping of users for permission assignment.                                                                                         |
| **Identity & Security**        | Configuration group governing identity and access.                                                                                   |
| **System Risk Controls**       | Dedicated configuration group for risk-related controls.                                                                             |
| **Audit Log**                  | Automatic recording of user activity and transaction changes.                                                                        |
| **Change Log**                 | Change log management.                                                                                                               |
| **System Logs**                | Configuration group covering system activity logging.                                                                                |
| **Backdate Configuration**     | Controls whether and how far back transactions may be dated - a direct answer to the "someone changed last month's numbers" problem. |
| **Approval Setup**             | Configuration of which transactions require approval and by whom.                                                                    |
| **Responsibility Transfer**    | Formal handover of responsibilities between users.                                                                                   |
| **Data Log / Data Log Report** | Transaction-level data logging in POS and elsewhere.                                                                                 |

## **8.4 How to sell the governance layer**

Governance is not usually what a buyer asks for. It is what they
discover they needed after something went wrong. The effective sales
move is to convert governance from an abstract feature into a specific
past incident.

- "Who approved that discount?" → Point Redeem and discount
  authorisation, with a system record.

- "Who changed last month's stock figure?" → Audit Log plus Backdate
  Configuration.

- "Why did we pay that supplier twice?" → Purchase Clear Invoice
  Approval plus the pending-invoice list.

- "Who let that customer go over their credit limit?" → Credit Limit
  Approval.

- "Who signed off this salary sheet?" → Salary Sheet Approval and Salary
  Advice Approval.

- "Who authorised this stock write-off?" → Stock Adjustment Approval and
  Asset Revaluation Approval.

For a group or multi-entity buyer, this is often the deciding
capability, ahead of any operational feature.

# **09. RTM (Route to Market) Deep Dive**

RTM is the distributor-to-market and secondary-sales execution layer. It
is a live module inside Managerium ERP, with its own dashboards, its own
approvals inside the Managerium approval dashboard, and its own field
mobile application.

## **9.1 The concepts, in plain language**

| **Term**                   | **Plain meaning**                                                                                                            |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Primary Sales**          | Product movement from the company, factory or central warehouse to a distributor or dealer.                                  |
| **Secondary Sales**        | Product movement from the distributor or dealer onward to retailers, outlets and the market.                                 |
| **RTM (Route to Market)**  | The operating route and control process through which products reach the market via distributors, sales teams and retailers. |
| **Sales Force Management** | Managing field representatives: attendance, market visits, targets, orders and performance.                                  |
| **Distributor Visibility** | Seeing distributor stock, orders, sales activity, delivery status and market coverage.                                       |
| **IMS**                    | In-Market Sales - what actually sold through into the market, as distinct from what was lifted by the distributor.           |

## **9.2 The core RTM argument**

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>The one-sentence RTM story</strong></p>
<p>Most companies can see what they shipped to their distributors. Very
few can see what happened after that. <strong>RTM is the answer to "what
happens after products reach distributors?"</strong></p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

The pain points that make this land:

- Management cannot clearly see what happens after products reach
  distributors.

- Secondary sales data arrives late, fragmented, or only through manual
  follow-up.

- Field attendance, route visits and sales activity are difficult to
  monitor consistently.

- Orders, distributor stock, delivery progress and team performance sit
  in separate places.

- Replenishment and sales decisions are made without a complete market
  picture.

- Sales leaders struggle to measure plan execution and KPI achievement.

## **9.4 RTM functional modules (from the iBOS RTM Solution overview)**

### **1. Salesforce Management**

| **Component**               | **Core inputs**                                                                                                                               | **Business purpose**                                                                                |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Salesforce Information**  | Basic: name, workplace, department, designation, grade, line manager, joining date. Personal: contact, religion, nationality, marital status. | Establishes organisational hierarchy, reporting lines and audit trails.                             |
| **Salesforce Route Setup**  | Date, day, category, tour location.                                                                                                           | Minimises field travel overheads by generating cost-effective, optimised routes.                    |
| **Salesforce Fixed TA/DA**  | Duration, designation, location parameters.                                                                                                   | Role- and location-based travel and daily allowance configuration.                                  |
| **Salesforce Target Setup** | Employee ID, specific sales targets, reward rules.                                                                                            | Incentivises performance by tracking action-oriented inputs rather than variable market conditions. |

### **2. Order Management**

| **Component**                | **Operational breakdown**                                                                                                                                        |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Outlet Management**        | Hierarchical grouping: **Territory → Route → Market → Outlet**. Supports dynamic outlet attributes and field-level customer surveys.                             |
| **Sales Target**             | Top-down revenue distribution across Departments → Groups → individual sales representatives.                                                                    |
| **Sales Order**              | Macro-level order construction using distribution channel, Strategic Business Unit (SBU), sold-to and ship-to party, pricing and shipping dates, and item lists. |
| **Sales Delivery**           | Shipping fulfilment logistics including shipping points, chalan numbers and ordered quantities.                                                                  |
| **Delivery Confirmation**    | Post-delivery workflow acting as an electronic ledger verification and date-filtered approval system for shipments.                                              |
| **Retail Order**             | Captures micro-level point-of-sale demand directly from outlets, or as pre-orders, categorised by distribution channel, distributor details and amounts.         |
| **Retail Delivery**          | Fulfils retail orders or pre-orders via flexible models: standard **Order Delivery** versus immediate **No-Order Direct Delivery**.                              |
| **Order Collection**         | Field forces execute cash and credit collection routines filtered by localised routes.                                                                           |
| **Damage Control**           | End-to-end stock quality tracking: Damage Type / Calendar Config → Field Entry → Target Rate Set → Multi-Level Approval Protocol.                                |
| **Stock Allocation**         | Uses analytical sales data to ration inventory ceilings to specific outlets, preventing artificial stockouts.                                                    |
| **Communication Management** | Broadcast engine pushing notifications to the field force about promotional products, price alterations and new launches.                                        |
| **Trade Offer**              | B2B promotion engine supporting volume-based or value-based rewards structured across tiered slabs or fixed product and amount conditions.                       |

### **3. Asset Management (in-market assets)**

| **Component**         | **Inputs**                                                          | **Workflow**                                               | **Purpose**                                                                            |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Asset Request**     | Max sales items, monthly sales average, target outlet profile.      | Field/Outlet initiates → Head Office reviews and approves. | Validates asset demand against real outlet performance to avoid wasteful distribution. |
| **Asset Allocation**  | Approved asset ID, assigned salesforce member, delivery parameters. | Head Office executes → Salesforce fulfils delivery.        | Formal deployment gateway transferring custodial tracking to a field representative.   |
| **Bill Request**      | Target outlet, cost itemisation, date parameters.                   | Field/Outlet submits.                                      | Captures operational and utility bills specific to maintaining presence at an outlet.  |
| **Bill Approval**     | Submitted bill records, verification logs, budget ceilings.         | Management/Admin authorises.                               | Financial clearinghouse for market-level outlet expenses.                              |
| **Asset Maintenance** | Complete asset details, cost type: amount or product-value swap.    | System/Service team records.                               | Tracks repairs; allows settling maintenance with cash or product replacement.          |
| **Asset Transfer**    | Transport information.                                              | Outlet → Head Office.                                      | Moves maintenance products back from the outlet.                                       |
| **Merchandising**     | Asset type, merchandising strategy, assignment log.                 | Merchandiser or Salesforce executes.                       | Uses brand assets to decorate the outlet, boosting visual trade presence.              |

### **4. Vehicle Management**

| **Component**         | **Attributes**                                                                      | **System dependencies and triggers**                                                                                                           |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Vehicle Profile**   | Vehicle info, driver data, distributor assignment, custodian or responsible person. | Base master data; populates active fleet selection.                                                                                            |
| **Vehicle Loading**   | Route tags, distributor tags, product line-item volumes, truck cubage capacity.     | Filters available trucks → locks inventory from warehouse → updates load status.                                                               |
| **Vehicle Unloading** | Trip completion logs, returned quantity, quality assessment (good versus damaged).  | **Auto-trigger:** updates central inventory count based on item quality. Good stock returns to inventory; damaged stock goes to damaged stock. |

### **5. Accounts and Finance (field)**

**Expense Management** - expense register, advance for internal expense,
receive entry and payment entry. Tracks ongoing field overheads such as
fuel, maintenance and gate fees against route profitability.

### **6. Human Capital Management (field)**

| **Component**         | **Actions**                                                                                      | **Configuration**                                                                                               | **Purpose**                                                                                         |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Leave & Movement**  | Employee leave requests, field movement logging, real-time application tracking.                 | Custom administrative workflows; role-dependent rules.                                                          | Simplifies the approval pipeline for administrators and employees, ensuring transparent scheduling. |
| **Attendance Report** | Standard on-site attendance, field and remote attendance check-ins, comprehensive daily reports. | Remote attendance parameters; geofencing or coordinate verification via the Remote Attendance Configure engine. | Automates capture of workforce log-ins across decentralised regions.                                |

## **9.5 RTM Corporate Dashboard**

The largest dashboard in the product. Filters by Year and Month, with
the active period shown explicitly. One observed tenant runs a
**21st-to-20th sales month** rather than a calendar month, confirming
that the sales cycle is configurable.

| **Panel**                          | **Contents**                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Analysis tabs**                  | Area Wise Analysis · Day-Wise Trend (30/31 Days) · Target vs Order Trend · Sales Order Delivery Forecast Trend · Order Delivery Actual. Charts support click-to-lock focus filtering.                                          |
| **360° Leaderboard**               | Toggles across **RSM / ASM / TSM** and **Top Products / Top Distributors / Top Officers**. Columns: name, Achievement, Target, Achievement %, Count, Rank with medal positions. Clicking an entry filters the whole dashboard. |
| **Layer wise contribution**        | Interactive performance graph, Target versus Achieved BDT across layers, with Both / Table / Charts and Bar / Pie toggles and a Collection Amount view.                                                                        |
| **Secondary Sales (as of)**        | Absolute Values (Order, Sales IMS, Collection against target) · Ratio Metrics (Target vs Order %, Target vs IMS %, Order vs IMS %, IMS vs Collection %) · Growth & De-Growth with sequential month-on-month.                   |
| **Primary Sales (as of)**          | Absolute Values (Order, Delivery, Deposit, Dues) · Ratio Metrics (Target vs Order %, Target vs Delivery %, Order vs Delivery %, Delivery vs Deposit %) · Growth & De-Growth.                                                   |
| **Layer wise pie chart drilldown** | Click a slice to drill into the next layer. Hierarchy: **Region → Area → Territory → Point → Section**, each with total target and percentage split.                                                                           |
| **FO Sales Clubbing**              | Field officer achievement bands: 0%, 1–20%, 21–50%, 51–80%, 81–100%+, with month-on-month counts and growth arrows.                                                                                                            |
| **DB Sales Clubbing**              | Distributor value bands: 0–3 Lac, 3–5 Lac, 5–10 Lac, 10–15 Lac, 15 Lac+, with month-on-month comparison.                                                                                                                       |


*The full RTM Corporate Dashboard - analysis tabs, 360° leaderboard,
layer-wise contribution, secondary and primary sales, ten KPI cards,
drilldown and sales clubbing.*

## **9.6 The ten RTM KPI cards - the strongest RTM asset**

This is a genuine FMCG secondary-sales KPI set. It is the vocabulary a
distribution or trade-marketing head already uses, and almost no local
ERP carries it. It should lead all RTM communication.

| **KPI card**                 | **Metrics inside it**                                                        | **What it answers**                                                                    |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **LIFTING**                  | Distributor Target · Lifting Order · Lifting Value · Time Pass · Achievement | Are distributors buying at the rate they committed to?                                 |
| **IMS**                      | Employee Target · IMS Order · IMS Value · Time Pass · Achievement            | Is stock actually selling through into the market, or just sitting at the distributor? |
| **PRODUCTIVITY**             | Schedule Call · Productive Call                                              | Are field visits producing orders?                                                     |
| **LPC & DROP SIZE**          | Total Line · Line Per Call · Drop Size · Total Amount                        | How many SKUs per visit, and how big is the average drop?                              |
| **OUTLET COVERAGE**          | Total Outlet · Unique Cover · Zero Transactions                              | How much of the outlet universe are we actually reaching?                              |
| **REQUIRED AVG DAILY SALES** | Target ADS · Current ADS · Required ADS                                      | At today's run rate, what do we need per day to still hit the month?                   |
| **VALUE PER CALL**           | Actual VPC · Order Value                                                     | What is a field visit worth?                                                           |
| **NUMERIC DISTRIBUTION**     | Route Universe · Buying Outlets · Non-Buying Outlets · ND Achievement        | What share of the route universe is buying?                                            |
| **HORIZONTAL EXPANSION**     | Base Outlets · New Registered · Prior New Registered · Active Route Growth % | Are we adding outlets, or just re-selling the same ones?                               |
| **STRIKE RATE**              | Physical Visits · Productive Orders · Non-Productive · Strike Rate           | What percentage of visits convert?                                                     |


*The ten RTM KPI cards with achievement rings.*


*Layer-wise pie chart drilldown - Region → Area → Territory → Point →
Section - with FO and DB sales clubbing bands beneath.*

## **9.7 RTM Sales Analytics**

### **Employee view**

Filters: Employee (single or All) · Channel · From Date · To Date · As
Of Date. Panels: Area Wise Analysis, Day-Wise Trend and Target vs Order
Trend tabs; a **SECONDARY** card (Target, Achievement, % of Achievement,
Collection, Market Credit, Discount); a **PRIMARY** card (Target, Order,
Delivery, Deposit, Dues); FO Order Clubbing by target percentage with
clickable rows; Attendance gauge with Total FO, Present and Absent;
Average Daily Memo; Memo Target percentage donut; and Today Sales
Performance showing Target, Order, Delivery and Collection.

### **Distributor view**

Filters: Distributor · Channel · From Date · To Date. Headline cards:
**MEMO** (target versus achievement), **B. RETAIL** (target versus
achievement), **VISIT** (target versus achievement), and **TODAY SALES**
(order, delivery, collection). Plus Primary and Secondary panels, an
As-Of Target versus Achievement donut, Top 10 Contribution by item, a
**Stock Items** panel showing stock quantity with **DP (Distributor
Price)** and **TP (Trade Price)** values per item, and a **Financial
Overview** giving total Stock at DP and total Stock at TP.

*Dual DP/TP valuation of distributor stock is a specific, nameable
capability. It answers "what is sitting at my distributors worth, at
cost and at trade?" - a question most systems cannot answer at all.*

- Food and beverage, FMCG and other high-volume distributor-led

- Organisations with large field-sales teams, multiple distributors and
  wide retail coverage.

- Businesses operating across multiple territories, regions or
  distribution channels.

- Manufacturers who sell through a distributor network and currently
  have no visibility past the depot gate.

## **9.10 RTM marketing direction**

RTM communication should start with operational pain, never with a
module list. The preferred story arc is: **"What happens after products
reach distributors?" → the field and distributor visibility gap → the
connected RTM flow → faster decisions, better market coverage, stronger
stock control and more accountable sales execution.**

## **10.3 Why the field app matters commercially**

| **Capability**                                         | **Objection it answers**                                                                                                                |
|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Offline Mode with explicit sync**                    | "Our field team works in areas with no reliable internet."                                                                              |
| **Map-based outlet coverage with status pins**         | "I can't tell whether my reps actually visited the outlets they claim."                                                                 |
| **QR scan at outlet, delivery and collection**         | "How do I know the visit really happened at the outlet?"                                                                                |
| **Gamification with badges and trophies**              | "My field team will not adopt a new app." Adoption is the real risk in field software; leaderboards and badges are the standard answer. |
| **Cascading Point → Section → Route → Market filters** | "Our territory structure is complicated."                                                                                               |
| **Order, delivery and collection in one app**          | "My reps carry three apps and a paper book."                                                                                            |

| **Furniture**              | High-value inventory, order tracking, branch transfer.                                                | Inventory, purchase, finance, customer management and reporting.                                                           |
| **Fuel / Forecourt**       | Fuel price changes, forecourt sales.                                                                  | Dedicated **Fuel Price Update** in the POS module. Currently unmarketed.                                                   |

| **Importers and import-dependent traders**                  | Foreign Purchase Order with shipment and charge conditions, LC Management, LC Margin, Intending Purchase.        | No page, no copy.                                      |

| **Project-based businesses**                                | Project Accounting, project-type purchase requisition, Cost Center.                                              | Mentioned nowhere in marketing.                        |

# **12. Business Problems Managerium Solves**

## **12.1 Pain-to-response mapping**

| **Business pain**                        | **Why it happens**                                                                                                 | **Managerium response**                                                                                                                    |
|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scattered data**                       | Different teams keep different records; there is no single source of truth.                                        | Connected database with module-based workflows and shared master data.                                                                     |
| **Stock mismatch**                       | Sales, purchase, returns, transfers and warehouse records do not agree.                                            | Transaction-linked inventory updates, stock adjustment with approval, audit setup and audit, gate in/out, transfer tracking.               |
| **Delayed reporting**                    | Management waits for Excel files, phone calls and manual follow-up.                                                | Module dashboards and structured reports available on demand, with Excel export and scheduled email delivery.                              |
| **Weak approval control**                | Purchases, expenses, transfers, discounts and credit decisions happen with limited visibility.                     | Approximately fifty approval types across nine groups, multilayer approval chains, permission groups and accountable user actions.         |
| **Finance disconnect**                   | Operations and finance re-enter or reconcile the same data separately.                                             | Integrated accounting with system-generated financial flow, bank reconciliation and the financial ratio view.                              |
| **Retail counter errors**                | Pricing, discounts, returns and barcode handling vary by staff member and outlet.                                  | POS with configured pricing, discount and offer rules, return exchange rules, negative sales configuration and counter permissions.        |
| **Growth chaos**                         | More outlets, departments, plants or warehouses increase coordination complexity faster than headcount can absorb. | Modular scaling with Business Unit, Office, Branch and Warehouse entities, and consolidated management visibility.                         |
| **Person dependency**                    | Critical reports and approvals depend on specific individuals.                                                     | Structured process, approval setup, responsibility transfer and system-based visibility reduce informal dependency.                        |
| **No visibility past the distributor**   | Secondary sales are reported manually, late, or not at all.                                                        | RTM with distributor stock, retail orders, delivery, collection and the full secondary-sales KPI set.                                      |
| **Procurement without discipline**       | Buying happens on relationship and habit rather than comparison and budget.                                        | Requisition → RFQ → Quotation Entry → Comparative Statement → Purchase Order, with approval at each stage and cycle-time analytics on top. |
| **After-sales falls through the cracks** | Complaints and service requests live in phone calls and WhatsApp.                                                  | POST CRM with complaint management, service requests, service agreements and reporting.                                                    |
| **Export paperwork chaos**               | LC, proforma, shipment schedules and export collections are tracked in spreadsheets.                               | Export Sales module with LC Management, Export LC Management and dedicated export approvals.                                               |

## **12.2 The strategic narrative**

Managerium should not be sold as "software with many modules". Its
stronger story is operational transformation, and it has four movements:

| **From**                       | **To**                                |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| **Manual growth**              | Controlled scale                      |
| **Scattered data**             | Structured data                       |
| **Follow-up-based management** | Report and dashboard-based visibility |
| **Person-dependent execution** | Defined, auditable process            |

# **13. Implementation & Adoption Journey**

Managerium implementation is framed as a business transformation journey
rather than a software installation. This framing matters commercially:
it is the honest answer to "how long will this take", and it is the
reason the 99% implementation success claim, if it can be substantiated,
is worth more than any feature.

## **13.1 The seven-stage method**

| **Stage**                     | **What happens**                                                                                          |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1. Assess Needs**           | Understand existing workflows, bottlenecks, stakeholders, required modules and business priorities.       |
| **2. Integrated Partnership** | Align AKIJ iBOS, management, department heads and end users on scope and ownership.                       |
| **3. System Blueprint**       | Map modules, roles, approvals, reports, integrations and data migration requirements.                     |
| **4. Configuration & Design** | Configure the system around actual business users and process reality, not around a generic template.     |
| **5. Data & Training**        | Prepare master data and train cashiers, store managers, operations, finance and leadership users by role. |
| **6. Pilot & Deployment**     | Validate key workflows, migrate, go live and support adoption.                                            |
| **7. Continuous Improvement** | Refine reports, workflows and adoption based on real usage.                                               |

*The live website presents this as six stages: Assess Needs · Integrated
Partnership · System Blueprint · Experience-Led Design · Deployment ·
Continuous Improvement. The seven-stage version above separates data and
training from deployment. Align the two before publishing either.*

## **13.2 Data preparation checklist**

The single largest cause of failed ERP go-lives is unprepared master
data. This checklist should be given to the client at blueprint stage,
not at go-live:

- Item master: SKU, item type classification, unit of measure, barcode,
  category and sub-category, item location.

- Price list: standard price, customer price, offer and discount rules,
  VAT treatment.

- Supplier master with payment terms and classification.

- Customer master with groups, credit limits and contact details.

- Opening stock by warehouse and location.

- Chart of accounts, cost centres and opening balances.

- Employee master, offices, business units, shifts, roster and leave
  quotas.

- User roles, permission groups and approval matrix.

- For manufacturing: BOMs with wastage percentages, work centres,
  equipment.

- For RTM: territory, route, market and outlet hierarchy, distribution
  channels, distributors, sales force structure and targets.

## **13.3 Role-based training map**

| **Role**                      | **What they need to be trained on**                                                                  |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cashier / counter staff**   | POS session, customer and item management, discount rules, payment, invoice, lock session.           |
| **Store / warehouse manager** | Requisition, issue, transfer, gate in/out, stock adjustment, audit.                                  |
| **Procurement officer**       | Requisition, RFQ, quotation entry, comparative statement, purchase order, receive, return, payment.  |
| **Finance / accounts**        | Journal, chart of accounts, expense and advance, budget, bank reconciliation, financial reports, LC. |
| **HR / payroll**              | Attendance, roster, leave, payroll run, salary generate, salary disbursement, separation.            |
| **Production supervisor**     | BOM, work centre, production order, production entry, material requirement.                          |
| **Field representative**      | Mobile app: attendance, journey, retail order, offline sync, delivery, collection, outlet report.    |
| **Approvers**                 | Approval dashboard, multilayer approval, what each approval type controls.                           |
| **Owner / management**        | Dashboards, reports, drilldown, export, and what to look at daily versus monthly.                    |

## **13.4 Adoption risks to manage**

- Poor data preparation or migration.

- Resistance to change, particularly where the old process protected
  someone's discretion.

- Insufficient role-based training.

- Attempting too much scope at once instead of phasing modules.

- Weak ownership from business leadership.

- Unclear process mapping before configuration.

- Unvalidated automation expectations - the client expecting alerts and
  automation that the current scope does not deliver.

- No post-go-live review, so early workarounds harden into permanent bad
  practice.

## **13.5 Phased adoption sequence (recommended)**

| **Phase**                        | **Modules**                                                      | **Why this order**                                                                                                                                    |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Phase 1 - Transactional core** | Purchase · Inventory · Sales (or POS for retail) · Configuration | These generate the data everything else depends on. Nothing downstream works until stock and transactions are clean.                                  |
| **Phase 2 - Financial close**    | Account · Approval · Multilayer Approval                         | Once transactions are reliable, finance can stop re-entering and start reconciling. Governance goes on at the same time so control habits form early. |
| **Phase 3 - Function depth**     | Payroll · Asset · Production · QC (as applicable)                | Departmental depth added after the backbone is stable.                                                                                                |
| **Phase 4 - Market extension**   | RTM · POST CRM · Export Sales (as applicable)                    | Outward-facing modules last, because they depend on clean item, price and customer master data.                                                       |

This is a strategic competitor shortlist, not a verified market-share

Where the buyer is RMG, counter with Sample, Tech Pack, Merchandiser Costing and export LC. |

| **Odoo**                                    | Global modular ERP   | Flexible apps and a large customisation ecosystem.                                       | Guided implementation, single-vendor accountability, local support and workflows that arrive connected rather than assembled.                                                         |

Total cost of ownership, not licence cost.                                                                        |

| **G-ERP / Smart ERP and similar**           | Local ERP            | Full-stack or manufacturing and distribution-focused local choices.                      | Brand trust, connected modules, implementation method and retail-to-enterprise breadth.                                                                                               |

## **15.2 Where Managerium wins**

| **Against**                              | **The winning argument**                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Global ERP (SAP, Dynamics, NetSuite)** | Cost, implementation proximity, local compliance understanding, and the fact that a Bangladeshi distribution or retail workflow does not have to be forced into a template designed elsewhere.    |
| **Open source (Odoo, ERPNext)**          | Single-vendor accountability. Someone answers the phone, owns the go-live and owns the fix. The comparison is not licence cost, it is who is responsible when it breaks.                          |
| **Local ERP**                            | Breadth. Very few local platforms carry POS, full accounting with LC, production with formulation and sampling, quality, after-sales service and a full RTM secondary-sales layer in one product. |
| **POS-only vendors**                     | POS handles counter sales. Managerium connects POS with purchase, stock, accounts, pricing, CRM, payroll and analytics.                                                                           |
| **Accounting-only vendors**              | Accounting records what already happened. Managerium controls what happens before it reaches accounting - requisition, approval, receipt, transfer.                                               |
| **Spreadsheets and status quo**          | The real competitor in most deals. Compete on the cost of the current process, not on features.                                                                                                   |

## **15.3 Where Managerium is currently exposed**

- **No published pricing** for Managerium ERP. Buyers who want to
  self-qualify cannot.

- **Under-described product.** A competitor comparison run off the live
  website would conclude Managerium has seven modules. It has fifteen.

- **Retail-skewed proof.** Every named testimonial is a retailer, which
  weakens the manufacturing and distribution pitch.

- **Unsubstantiated efficiency claim.** A 300% figure invites challenge
  from a sophisticated buyer and can damage credibility on everything
  else.

- **No technology stack disclosed.** The site shows eighteen unnamed
  technology logos. IT buyers want names.

- **No security or certification detail** attached to the certification
  marks in the footer.

# **16. Sales Enablement & Buyer Messaging**

## **16.1 Discovery questions**

These are ordered to move from symptom to cost to consequence. The goal
is not to qualify the buyer for Managerium; it is to make the buyer
describe their own problem out loud.

1.  How many software tools, spreadsheets or manual registers are used
    across sales, inventory, finance and purchase?

2.  How often do stock records mismatch between counter, warehouse and
    accounts? What happens when they do?

3.  How long does it take management to receive daily sales, stock and
    receivable reports?

4.  Can the business identify fast-moving, slow-moving and dead stock
    quickly?

5.  Can management see branch or outlet profit, performance and stock
    position without calling several people?

6.  Are purchase orders, approvals and supplier payments connected with
    accounts?

7.  Who can approve a discount, a write-off or a credit-limit exception
    today, and where is that recorded?

8.  How much decision-making depends on one or two key employees? What
    happens when they are unavailable?

9.  If five more outlets or units open, will the current process scale
    smoothly?

10. For distribution: what do you actually know about what happens after
    your products reach your distributors?

11. For manufacturing: how do you currently measure wastage and yield
    against the BOM?

12. For exporters: how are LC, proforma and shipment schedules tracked
    today?

## **16.2 Persona messaging**

| **Persona**                   | **Primary concern**                                                     | **Message direction**                                                                     |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Owner / MD**                | Control, visibility, profit protection, less dependence on individuals. | See the business from one system before leakage becomes loss.                             |
| **CFO / Accounts Head**       | Transaction accuracy, AR/AP, reconciliation, audit readiness.           | Finance should receive structured operational data instead of chasing it.                 |
| **COO / Operations Head**     | Purchase, warehouse, production, sales and delivery discipline.         | When departments work in one system, operations become measurable.                        |
| **Retail Head**               | POS, branch stock, pricing, returns, discounts, customer insight.       | From counter to management dashboard, activity stays connected.                           |
| **IT Head / CIO**             | Security, scalability, configurability, supportability.                 | A modern ERP with modules, controls, permissions and implementation support.              |
| **Distribution / Sales Head** | Market execution, distributor stock, field team, secondary sales.       | See what happens after products reach distributors and keep field execution accountable.  |
| **Factory / Production Head** | Yield, wastage, machine utilisation, material availability.             | Every unit produced and every material consumed, tracked the moment it happens.           |
| **Commercial / Export Head**  | LC, shipment schedules, proforma, export collection.                    | Export documentation and trade finance inside the same system as the stock it relates to. |

## **16.3 Objection handling**

| **Objection**                                | **Response**                                                                                                                                                    | **Caution**                                                                      |
|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **"ERP is too advanced for my team."**       | Position guided onboarding, role-based training and phased module adoption. Most users only ever see the four or five screens their job needs.                  | Do not quote a specific learning time until it is validated.                     |
| **"Employees will struggle to learn it."**   | Organised menus, favourites for daily screens, global search, documentation and training. The live FAQ says most users understand the basics within a few days. | That FAQ claim is live on the website; keep the two consistent.                  |
| **"We already have a POS."**                 | POS handles counter sales. Managerium connects POS with purchase, stock, accounts, pricing, CRM, payroll and analytics.                                         | -                                                                                |
| **"We have multiple outlets."**              | Central branch and outlet dashboards, stock transfer with tracking, and consolidated visibility.                                                                | -                                                                                |
| **"Our main problem is stock mismatch."**    | Transaction-linked stock movement, stock adjustment with approval, audit setup and audit, gate in/out and warehouse controls. Then show Coverage Days.          | -                                                                                |
| **"Our internet is unstable."**              | The RTM field app has explicit offline mode with sync. Retail offline behaviour varies by package.                                                              | Confirm the exact package behaviour before promising anything about POS offline. |
| **"We need local requirements - VAT, NBR."** | Bangladesh-ready workflow, Tax Management, VAT discount handling at POS and VAT reporting.                                                                      | Confirm the exact scope of VAT and NBR support before committing.                |
| **"What if it doesn't work out?"**           | Phased implementation, pilot before scale-up, and a documented seven-stage method.                                                                              | -                                                                                |
| **"How much?"**                              | Managerium ERP is scoped and quoted per engagement. Move to a discovery conversation.                                                                           | There is no published ERP price list. Do not invent one.                         |
| **"Who else in my industry uses it?"**       | Name the verified references for their sector.                                                                                                                  | Only use customers cleared in Section 14.2. Do not name unconfirmed accounts.    |

## **16.4 Recommended demo flow**

A demo that opens with the module list loses. A demo that opens with the
buyer's own question wins. Recommended sequence:

1.  **Start on the main dashboard.** Ask them what they normally have to
    phone someone to find out. Show it on screen.

2.  **Show one transaction end to end** in their language - for a
    trader, requisition through comparative statement to purchase order;
    for a retailer, a counter sale updating stock and the ledger.

3.  **Show the approval that transaction triggered**, with the pending
    count on the approval dashboard.

4.  **Show the analytical layer they did not expect** - procurement
    cycle time, coverage days, or the financial ratio table.

5.  **Show the mobile view**, especially for distribution buyers.

6.  **Close on the implementation method**, not on features. The last
    thing they should remember is that someone owns the go-live.

## **16.5 Live website FAQ - current answers**

These are already public and must stay consistent with anything said in
sales:

| **Question**                                                                             | **Current live answer**                                                                                                                                                                             |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| I run a small team. Is Managerium too advanced for us?                                   | Built for everyday use. Even with a small team, manage sales, stock, purchases, accounts and approvals in one place. Simple enough for daily operations, powerful enough to grow with the business. |
| I have multiple outlets. Will Managerium show all sales and stock together in real time? | Yes. One central dashboard showing outlet-wise sales, current stock, fast and slow-moving items and daily activities. No separate software or manual reports needed.                                |
| How hard is it for employees to learn the system?                                        | Most users understand the basics within a few days. Clean interface, menus organised by module, and AKIJ iBOS provides onboarding support, user training and documentation.                         |
| Can Managerium fix my stock mismatch issues?                                             | Yes. Stock updates instantly after every sale, purchase, return or transfer, plus stock adjustment tools, warehouse controls and item tracking.                                                     |
| Does the ERP include POS features for retail billing?                                    | Yes. A fast and reliable POS module: billing, discounts, barcode scanning, returns, exchanges and outlet-level sales reports directly from the ERP.                                                 |

## **17.3 Authority content territories**

- Growth without control becomes leakage.

- From Excel to ERP: the point where tracking stops scaling.

- The hidden cost of stock mismatch.

- Your business should not depend on one employee.

- Real-time dashboards are not a luxury when decisions depend on them.

- POS is not enough for a multi-function retail operation.

- Owner control without micromanagement.

- ERP implementation is a business transformation, not an IT project.

- Inventory distortion, profit leakage, delayed data, reconciliation and
  approval gaps.

- What happens after products reach distributors? (RTM)

- Procurement without comparison is procurement without margin.
  (Purchase analytics)

- Coverage days: the number that tells you when you will actually run
  out. (Inventory)

- Standard ratio versus your ratio: reading your own balance sheet.
  (Financial ratio analysis)

- Fifty approvals: what governance actually looks like inside a
  business. (Approval layer)

# **19. Visual & Copy System**

## **19.1 Documented visual direction**

- Strong white space and a clear visual hierarchy.

- Managerium Blue and Deep Navy as the main identity, with Digital Red
  as a controlled CTA accent.

- Professional offices, factories, warehouses, retail outlets, pharmacy
  counters and meeting rooms.

- Real decision-makers and teams using dashboards and connected
  workflows.

- Dashboard cards, process maps, workflow lines and reporting graphics
  where they clarify the message.

- Social formats: 1:1 and 4:5 for feed, 9:16 for Reels and Stories, 16:9
  for video.

## **19.2 Working creative direction**

## **19.3 Copy characteristics**

- Simple, complete sentences - not fragments stacked for visual effect.

- Premium but plain Bangla-English mix; common business and software
  words may stay in English.

- Headlines should normally communicate one concrete business situation
  or benefit.

- Avoid generic "smarter / faster / control" language unless tied to a
  specific operation.

- For authoritative content, lead with a business insight or
  research-backed problem, then connect Managerium naturally.

- For RTM, "Control-এ" is preferred over the vaguer "নজরে" when the
  intended message is operational control.

- Name the module when naming it makes the claim more credible.
  "Comparative Statement" is more convincing than "smart buying".

## **19.4 Headline patterns that already work**

These patterns are established across the live industry pages and should
be reused rather than reinvented:

- **"Manage Your \[X\] in One Place"** - plain, operational, works
  across every industry.

- **"Give Your \[X\] the \[Control / Organization / Operating System\]
  It Deserves"** - the long-form block header.

- **"Managerium: Your \[X\] Growth Enabler"** - the benefit-tile block
  header.

- **"Smart Tools to Make \[X\] Management Simple"** - the alternative
  feature-block header.

*Two competing section systems currently run across the six pages. Pick
one and standardise. See Section 04.4.*

## **19.5 Words and claims to avoid**

| **Avoid**                                                                    | **Why**                                                     | **Use instead**                                                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **"Automatic expiry alerts" / "automatic reorder notifications" (pharmacy)** | Directly contradicts the August 2026 pharmacy scope master. | "Batch-wise expiry visibility in inventory reports" / "review stock and raise a purchase requisition". |
| **"Predictive analysis"**                                                    | No evidence of predictive analytics in the product.         | "Real-time insight" or "trend analysis".                                                               |
| **"300% boost in efficiency"**                                               | Unsubstantiated performance claim.                          | A specific, sourced customer outcome, or nothing.                                                      |
| **"Fully automated"**                                                        | Automation scope varies by module and configuration.        | Name the specific automated step, e.g. "vehicle unloading updates stock automatically".                |
| **"Cloud based" vs "on premise" absolutes**                                  | Delivery model wording has varied across documents.         | "Cloud-based web application with mobile access", once confirmed.                                      |
| **"Managerium Pharmacy" / "Managerium POS" as product names**                | These are not products.                                     | "Managerium for pharmacy businesses" / "the POS module in Managerium".                                 |
| **"For retailers" on ERP-level assets**                                      | Narrows an all-industry product.                            | "For businesses" or "for organisations".                                                               |

This is a contractual promise.                                                                          |

# **01. Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)**

PeopleDesk primarily serves organisations that need to move from
fragmented, manual and people-dependent HR operations to one connected,
automated and decision-ready HRM platform.

## **ICP Questions**

| **Question**                            | **Answer**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Who Are They?**                       | HR Teams, Admin Teams, Payroll Teams, Finance Teams, Department Heads, CXOs, SMEs, multi-branch companies, factories, retailers, service companies, field-force businesses and large enterprises.                                                |
| **What Do They Currently Think?**       | They believe HR can still be managed through Excel, manual attendance, biometric data, paperwork, scattered employee files and manual payroll. They may also think HRMS is complex, costly or difficult for employees to adopt.                  |
| **What Problem Do They Face?**          | Manual attendance correction, payroll errors, leave approval delays, scattered employee information, shift and roster confusion, field-force attendance control issues and a lack of real-time HR reporting.                                     |
| **What Do We Want Them To Think?**      | PeopleDesk is not just HR software. It is an AI-driven HRM system that connects attendance, leave, payroll, employee records, shift, roster, GPS attendance and HR reports in one platform.                                                      |
| **What Action Do We Want?**             | Book a demo, schedule a call, audit the current HR process and explore how PeopleDesk can automate attendance-to-payroll operations.                                                                                                             |
| **What Proof Will Convince Them?**      | Automated attendance, leave-payroll sync, GPS attendance, shift scheduling, centralised employee records, HR reports, 24/7 support, 99% successful HR and payroll implementation, 30k+ employees managed daily and trust from 50+ organisations. |
| **What Tone Should We Use?**            | Practical, problem-solving, HR-friendly, confidence-building, simple and business-focused. Communication should speak clearly to HR, Finance and CXO-level decision-makers.                                                                      |
| **Which Channels Will Influence Them?** | LinkedIn, Facebook, HR community groups, YouTube explainers, webinars, email campaigns, sales decks, demo sessions, case studies, retargeting ads and direct CXO or HR Head outreach.                                                            |

## **ICP Priority Segments**

| **Priority**               | **Definition**                                                                                                                                                                       |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Primary**                | HR Heads, HR Operations, Payroll and Admin teams in companies with recurring attendance, shift, leave and payroll complexity.                                                        |
| **Economic Buyers**        | CXOs, Business Owners, CFOs, CHROs and Heads of HR who control budgets, risk and transformation decisions.                                                                           |
| **High-fit Organisations** | Factories, multi-branch companies, retailers, field-force organisations, service companies and enterprises managing large or distributed teams.                                      |
| **Trigger Events**         | Rapid headcount growth, new branches, payroll errors, policy inconsistency, biometric limitations, audit pressure, high HR workload or leadership demand for live workforce reports. |

# **02. Brand Guideline**

***Brand Essence: PeopleDesk turns everyday HR complexity into a simple,
connected and intelligent people-management experience.***

## **2.1 Brand Overview**

| **Brand Purpose** | Simplify people operations through a smart, reliable and easy-to-use HRM platform that helps organisations manage employees accurately, reduce manual work and make better workforce decisions.                                             |
| **Mission**       | Deliver a scalable, cloud-based and AI-driven HRM system that connects employee data, attendance, leave, payroll, shift, roster, performance, training, assets, expenses, approvals and reports with dependable implementation and support. |
| **Vision**        | Become the trusted people operating system for growing organisations by making HR management simple, connected, employee-friendly and future-ready.                                                                                         |
| **Core Values**   | Simplicity, accuracy, reliability, empathy, transparency, innovation, practical excellence, employee experience, client commitment and long-term value creation.                                                                            |

## **2.2 Brand Positioning**

| **Target Audience**          | HR, Admin, Payroll, Finance and CXO teams in SMEs, factories, service companies, retailers, multi-branch businesses, field-force operations and large enterprises.         |
| **Unique Value Proposition** | One AI-driven HRM platform that connects attendance, leave, payroll, employee records, shifts, rosters, GPS attendance, self-service, performance and real-time reporting. |
| **Brand Promise**            | PeopleDesk makes people operations simpler, more accurate and more visible by connecting every core HR workflow in one reliable platform.                                  |
| **Key Message**              | One intelligent HRM platform for accurate payroll, connected employees and complete workforce visibility.                                                                  |

## **2.3 Brand Personality, Voice & Tone**

| **Brand Personality**   | Sage + Creator with a people-first spirit: intelligent, dependable, clear, empathetic, practical, modern, confident and solution-driven.                                                                     |
| **Communication Style** | Clear, HR-friendly, educational, supportive and business-focused. Explain the operational problem, employee impact, solution and measurable value without making the message technical or intimidating.      |
| **Language Guidelines** | Use simple business English and natural Bangla where relevant. Keep familiar HR and software terms in English. Use short sentences, active voice and consistent naming such as “PeopleDesk HRM”.             |
| **Do**                  | Focus on attendance accuracy, payroll confidence, employee experience, faster approvals, visibility, automation and scalable HR operations. Use real workflows, dashboards, proof points and client stories. |
| **Don’t**               | Do not shame HR teams, overpromise, use excessive jargon, show unrealistic employee behaviour, clutter layouts, use fear-only messaging or publish unverified statistics.                                    |

## **2.4 Logo Guidelines**


*PeopleDesk primary multicolour symbol + wordmark (source: Features &
Modules PDF, Google Drive brand asset folder linked in internal doc)*

| **Primary & Alternative Logo** | Use the full-colour horizontal logo on white or very light backgrounds. Use a white/reversed wordmark version on Deep Navy backgrounds. Use the multicolour symbol-only mark for app icons, favicons and compact digital placements. Use monochrome only when production limitations require it. |
| **Clear Space**                | Keep minimum clear space equal to the diameter of one outer circular node around every side of the logo. Recommended standard; confirm against the master logo grid.                                                                                                                             |
| **Minimum Size**               | Full logo: minimum 150 px wide (digital) / 40 mm (print). Symbol-only: minimum 32 px (digital) / 10 mm (print). Test legibility before final approval.                                                                                                                                           |
| **Correct Usage**              | Preserve proportions, original colours, symbol-wordmark spacing and strong background contrast. Prefer white backgrounds for the full-colour logo.                                                                                                                                               |
| **Incorrect Usage**            | Do not stretch, rotate, recolour, crop, rearrange the people symbol, remove any colour node, add shadows/outlines, use on busy backgrounds, or recreate the wordmark by typing.                                                                                                                  |
| **Brand Asset Folder**         | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1M9VpXx3BtAkXpqEWT9UWNFPuR8qOElBK?usp=drive_link (internal - access required)                                                                                                                                                                             |

## **2.5 Colour Palette**

Recommended usage: 55–60% White, 25–30% Deep Navy, and 10–15% combined
PeopleDesk accent colours. Use Green for positive outcomes, Blue for
digital actions and links, Yellow for attention/energy, and Red for
urgent actions or small emphasis only.

|            | **People Green**  | \#34A853 | 52, 168, 83   | 69, 0, 51, 34 |
|            | **People Red**    | \#EA4335 | 234, 67, 53   | 0, 71, 77, 8  |
|            | **People Yellow** | \#FBBC05 | 251, 188, 5   | 0, 25, 98, 2  |
|            | **People Blue**   | \#4285F4 | 66, 133, 244  | 73, 45, 0, 4  |
|            | **White**         | \#FFFFFF | 255, 255, 255 | 0, 0, 0, 0    |

## **2.6 Typography**

| **Primary Font**        | Poppins - English marketing communication, presentations, website content and corporate layouts.                       |
| **Secondary / UI Font** | Roboto - product interfaces, dashboards, mobile app and desktop application text.                                      |
| **Bangla Font**         | Hind Siliguri or Ador Noirrit, depending on readability and design context.                                            |
| **Heading Style**       | Poppins SemiBold/Bold; concise, benefit-led and easy to scan. Prefer sentence case or consistent title case.           |
| **Body Text Style**     | Poppins Regular/Medium; short paragraphs, clear hierarchy and comfortable spacing. Keep technical explanations simple. |

## **2.7 Visual Style**

| **Photography / Illustration** | Show HR professionals, managers, employees and field teams in offices, factories, retail branches, service locations and mobile-work contexts. Professional, approachable, organised, people-centred. Use corporate cartoon, 3D or isometric illustration when it helps simplify HR workflows. |
| **Product Visuals**            | Prioritise dashboards, employee profiles, attendance maps, leave and approval flows, payroll summaries, shift rosters, KPI cards, reports and mobile self-service screens.                                                                                                                     |
| **Icon & Graphic Style**       | One consistent family of simple geometric icons. The four PeopleDesk colours may represent connected HR pillars or employee touchpoints. Avoid mixed icon families and decorative shapes without functional meaning.                                                                           |
| **Layout Direction**           | Clean corporate composition, strong white space, F/Z hierarchy: people problem/insight first → workflow/dashboard second → business benefit third → CTA last.                                                                                                                                  |
| **Logo Placement**             | For AKIJ iBOS product communication: AKIJ iBOS top-left, PeopleDesk top-right. Never place logos at the bottom of marketing content.                                                                                                                                                           |

## **2.8 Key Brand Applications**

| **Social Media**              | 1:1 and 4:5 for feed, 9:16 for Reels/Stories, 16:9 for YouTube. Follow Hook → Problem → Narrative → Solution → CTA. Use HR workflow visuals, short benefit-led copy, consistent top-corner logo placement. |
| **Business Card**             | White-based, clean, premium; Deep Navy as main identity, multicolour accents used sparingly. Include “A Product of AKIJ iBOS” where appropriate.                                                           |
| **Letterhead**                | White base, clear logo placement, generous writing space, neat contact details, Deep Navy anchor strip. Coloured elements minimal and professional.                                                        |
| **Email Signature**           | Logo left, information right, separated by a thin vertical divider. Deep Navy for name, Greystone for designation/body, People Blue for links, one small multicolour/Green accent.                         |
| **Presentation / Sales Deck** | Problem-to-outcome narrative: current HR challenge → operational impact → PeopleDesk workflow → proof → implementation → CTA.                                                                              |

## **2.9 Approval Notes (Open Items)**

| **Logo Clear Space**  | Recommended as one outer-circle diameter on all sides. Confirm against the final master logo grid.                                      |
| **Minimum Logo Size** | Recommended as 150 px / 40 mm (full logo) and 32 px / 10 mm (symbol). Confirm through application testing.                              |
| **Colour Codes**      | Digital colours extracted from the provided logo artwork. CMYK output should be validated through printed proof before bulk production. |
