# **04. Product Details**

***Core Positioning: PeopleDesk is an AI-driven, cloud-based HRM and
payroll platform that connects attendance, leave, payroll, employee
records, shift, roster, self-service, performance and reporting in one
intelligent system.***

## **4.1 Product at a Glance**

| **Product Name**           | PeopleDesk                                                                                                           |
| **Company**                | AKIJ iBOS Ltd.                                                                                                       |
| **Product Category**       | AI-driven HRM, HRIS and Payroll Management Platform                                                                  |
| **Primary Promise**        | Replace scattered HR data, manual corrections and delayed approvals with one connected employee-management system.   |
| **Best-Fit Organisations** | SMEs, factories, retailers, multi-branch companies, field-force businesses, service companies and large enterprises. |
| **Primary CTA**            | Book a Demo / Schedule a Call / Audit Current HR Process                                                             |
| **Public Trust Signals**   | 24/7 support, 99% successful HR and payroll implementation, 30k+ employees managed daily, 50+ client organisations.  |

## **4.2 Business Problems PeopleDesk Solves**

| **Problem**                        | **Without a Connected HRMS**                                                           | **PeopleDesk Response**                                                                                 |
|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Attendance correction overload     | Manual attendance, device data and employee requests require repeated HR corrections.  | Automated check-in/out, attendance rules, mobile/GPS attendance, rosters and structured regularisation. |
| Payroll errors and delayed salary  | Attendance, leave, overtime, bonuses and deductions are calculated in separate files.  | Attendance and leave data sync with payroll, allowances, deductions, bonuses and salary generation.     |
| Leave and approval delays          | Requests move through email, paper or messages without clear status.                   | Unified approval workflows for leave, loans, expenses, movement, assets and HR requests.                |
| Scattered employee records         | Documents, history, transfers and policy information stay in folders and spreadsheets. | Central employee lifecycle records covering joining, confirmation, transfers, profile and separation.   |
| Shift and roster confusion         | Factories, retail teams and service operations struggle with rotating schedules.       | Shift planning, roster management, attendance rules and timesheet visibility.                           |
| Field-force visibility gap         | Management cannot confirm remote or market-visit attendance accurately.                | GPS attendance, location checks, movement requests and mobile employee self-service.                    |
| Weak management reporting          | HR reports are delayed and leadership lacks live workforce visibility.                 | Dashboard suites and real-time reports across attendance, payroll, performance and employee data.       |
| Inconsistent performance appraisal | KPI, behavioural assessment and evaluation vary by manager.                            | Performance goals, KPI/BAR evaluation, appraisals and yearly performance reports.                       |

## **4.3 Core HRM Modules (Summary)**

| **Module**              | **What It Covers**                                                                               | **Business Value**                                            |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Administration          | Central setup for policies, roles, shifts, holidays, rules and system configuration.             | Creates consistency across HR operations.                     |
| Attendance & Leave      | Attendance, leave rules, rosters, timesheets, IN/OUT, regularisation, location-based attendance. | Improves attendance accuracy and reduces manual correction.   |
| Payroll & Compensation  | Salary structures, allowances, deductions, bonuses, overtime, salary generation.                 | Connects real attendance data with accurate payroll.          |
| Employee Management     | Joining, onboarding, confirmation, transfer, employee history, documents, lifecycle records.     | Creates one reliable employee database.                       |
| Employee Self-Service   | Payslips, leave, expenses, requests, profile updates, documents, employee-facing actions.        | Reduces HR dependency and improves employee experience.       |
| Approval Workflow       | Leave, payroll, loans, expenses, assets, requisitions and other multi-level approvals.           | Speeds up decisions and creates transparent status tracking.  |
| Performance Management  | KPI, BAR, goals, appraisal, evaluation, skill-gap and annual performance reporting.              | Supports fairer assessment and measurable development.        |
| Training & Development  | Training plans, calendars, requisitions, participation and development tracking.                 | Links skill gaps with learning and performance growth.        |
| Loan & PF Management    | Provident fund, loans, advances, repayment and lifecycle tracking.                               | Reduces calculation errors and improves financial discipline. |
| Expense & Movement      | Expense claims, market visits, movement requests, TADA and approvals.                            | Improves visibility for field and travelling employees.       |
| Asset Management        | Register, assign, transfer, maintain and recover company assets.                                 | Strengthens accountability across the asset lifecycle.        |
| Organogram & Structure  | Visual hierarchy, departments, designations and reporting lines.                                 | Clarifies organisational structure and authority.             |
| Retirement & Settlement | Exit, clearance, final settlement and retirement workflows.                                      | Creates a controlled, auditable separation process.           |
| Notification & Logs     | Alerts, notices, attendance logs and workflow activity.                                          | Keeps users informed and improves traceability.               |
| Reports & Analytics     | Real-time HR, attendance, leave, payroll, performance and workforce reports.                     | Gives HR and leadership faster decision support.              |
| Dashboard Suite         | Employee, supervisor, HR and management dashboards.                                              | Provides role-based visibility and control.                   |

## **4.4 Smart, Mobile & AI Capabilities**

| **GPS / Geofenced Attendance** | Confirm attendance and field activity through approved location checks for remote and outdoor employees.                                                           |
| **Mobile Face Attendance**     | Employees can register and submit attendance through mobile face recognition without depending only on a separate attendance device, subject to configured policy. |
| **PeopleDesk Mobile App**      | Employee self-service for attendance, leave, regularisation, payslips, profile information, requests and approvals.                                                |
| **AI-Driven HR Support**       | AI-assisted HR experience can answer employee questions and guide routine HR actions through an intelligent assistant layer.                                       |
| **Smart Document Generation**  | Generate HR documents such as NOC, salary certificates, offer, promotion and increment letters through structured templates and workflows.                         |
| **Real-Time Dashboards**       | Provide role-based insight to employees, supervisors, HR and management without waiting for manual reports.                                                        |

| **24/7 Support**                 | Dedicated support access for client issues, guidance and operational continuity.          |
| **99% Implementation Success**   | Publicly stated successful HR and payroll implementation rate across multiple industries. |
| **30k+ Employees Managed Daily** | Demonstrates scale across attendance, payroll, employee records and daily HR activity.    |
| **50+ Organisations**            | Public trust signal showing adoption across multiple sectors.                             |

| **Service Company**         | Employee records, attendance, leave, payroll, performance, expenses and management dashboards.                                |
| **SME / Growing Company**   | Replace Excel and manual HR with central records, ESS, attendance, payroll and scalable workflows.                            |
| **Large Enterprise**        | Complex structure, multi-level approval, performance, training, assets, analytics, integration and implementation governance. |

## **4.7 Implementation Journey**

| **1. HR Process Audit**            | Map current attendance, leave, payroll, policies, approvals, devices, locations and reporting pain.                         |
| **2. Solution Blueprint**          | Define modules, roles, organisation structure, payroll rules, shifts, reports, integrations and rollout scope.              |
| **3. Data Preparation**            | Prepare employee master data, policies, salary structures, opening balances, leave data, attendance devices and user roles. |
| **4. Configuration & Integration** | Configure workflows, payroll, mobile/GPS attendance, biometric integration, dashboards and security permissions.            |
| **5. Training & Pilot**            | Train HR, payroll, managers and employees; run pilot attendance and payroll cycles.                                         |
| **6. Go-Live**                     | Launch agreed modules with implementation and support coverage.                                                             |
| **7. Optimisation**                | Review adoption, reporting, exceptions, automation opportunities and additional module rollout.                             |

## **4.8 Messaging Guide**

| **Core Positioning Statement** | PeopleDesk is an AI-driven HRM platform that connects attendance, leave, payroll, employee records, shift, roster, self-service, performance and reporting into one reliable system. |
| **Primary Sales Hook**         | Your HR team should manage people, not spend every month correcting attendance and rebuilding payroll in Excel.                                                                      |
| **Leadership Message**         | See workforce activity, payroll readiness and HR performance without depending on manual follow-ups.                                                                                 |
| **HR Message**                 | Automate repetitive HR tasks and keep every employee workflow organised from joining to final settlement.                                                                            |
| **Finance Message**            | Connect attendance, leave, overtime and salary rules to reduce payroll errors and reconciliation work.                                                                               |
| **Employee Message**           | Access attendance, leave, payslips, requests and HR information through a simple self-service experience.                                                                            |

## **Competitive Positioning Principles**

- Do not compete only on the number of features. Compete on connected
  workflows, adoption, implementation reliability and measurable HR
  outcomes.

- Use attendance-to-payroll accuracy, employee self-service, mobile/GPS
  attendance, performance, reports and support as the core comparison
  pillars.

- Avoid attacking competitors directly. Show the operational difference
  through use cases, dashboards, implementation plans and customer
  proof.

- Create separate comparison sheets for factories, multi-branch
  companies, field-force businesses and large enterprises because their
  buying priorities differ.

## **12-Month Channel Roadmap**

| **Phase 1: Foundation (0–3 months)**          | Google Search, LinkedIn ABM, conversion tracking, process-audit lead magnet, segmented landing pages, webinar calendar and email nurture.       |
| **Phase 2: Authority & Nurture (3–6 months)** | PeopleDesk Academy, customer stories, HR community partnerships, referral programme, industry-specific sales kits and monthly demo days.        |
| **Phase 3: Scale & Expansion (6–12 months)**  | Marketplace reviews, integration partnerships, vertical events, international content, partner channels and account-based enterprise campaigns. |

## **Channel Measurement Framework**

| **Awareness**      | Reach, video views, branded search, follower growth and target-account engagement.                    |
| **Demand**         | Landing-page conversions, webinar registrations, audit requests, qualified inbound and demo bookings. |
| **Quality**        | MQL-to-SQL rate, ICP fit, company size, industry, workforce size and urgency.                         |
| **Sales Progress** | Demo completion, proposal rate, sales cycle, pipeline value and close rate by channel.                |
| **Efficiency**     | Cost per qualified lead, customer acquisition cost, conversion rate and revenue/ROMI attribution.     |

# **01. Product Identity & Positioning**

## **1.1 What Managerium Retail ERP is**

**Managerium Retail ERP** is AKIJ iBOS's retail-focused edition of the
Managerium platform. It is positioned as an end-to-end retail operating
system that connects the front counter with back-office control: POS,
purchase, stock, accounts, pricing, outlet activity, payroll, CRM and
analytics operate within one connected platform rather than as separate
tools.

The core business promise is not simply faster billing. It is to reduce
scattered operations and manual errors by connecting retail counters,
inventory, purchase, finance, customer activity and management
visibility into a single operating structure.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p><strong>Retail ERP in one line</strong></p>
<p>Your retail business is not only a counter. It is sales, stock,
purchase, accounts, people, customers and outlets - Managerium connects
them.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Built for retail businesses of every kind - single outlet, multi-counter, chain, super shop, pharmacy, fashion, footwear, restaurant, bakery, electronics, furniture. | ibos.io/retail-erp/        | **This document.** Primary subject.                                                                                     |

Has its own separate master document, referenced here for module and brand depth. |

Out of scope for this document.                                                                       |

## **1.3 Product promise**

- Bring sales, stock, accounts, pricing and outlet activity into one
  connected system.

- Connect front-counter POS activity with purchase, inventory and
  finance instead of maintaining separate tools.

- Give management real-time or structured dashboard visibility across
  sales, inventory, finance, customers and outlets, subject to module
  and configuration scope.

- Scale from smaller retail operations to multi-counter, multi-outlet
  and enterprise-level needs through modular packages and configuration.

## **1.4 Core value pillars**

| **Pillar**      | **Retail meaning**                                                                                                                       |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Visibility**  | Dashboard and report access for sales, inventory, outlet and financial performance.                                                      |
| **Accuracy**    | Structured transactions, barcode/POS discipline, stock updates, audits and fewer manual mismatches.                                      |
| **Control**     | Permissions, pricing rules, returns, stock movement, approvals and outlet-level management.                                              |
| **Speed**       | Faster billing, reporting, approvals and day-to-day retail decision-making.                                                              |
| **Scalability** | Supports growth from one outlet to multi-counter, multi-outlet and enterprise operations.                                                |
| **Support**     | Implementation, onboarding and support are part of the overall Managerium value story; public SLA claims should be validated before use. |

## **1.5 Strategic differentiation**

- Retail depth beyond POS: counter + inventory + purchase + accounts +
  pricing + customer + people + analytics in one platform.

- Bangladesh-ready operating context, including local VAT-related add-on
  capability and practical retail workflows.

- Connected business-control narrative for owners, CXOs and operations
  leaders - not feature-only technical messaging.

- Scalable package architecture (Standard → Professional → Premium →
  Enterprise) with a clear enterprise customisation path.

- Backed by AKIJ iBOS's broader platform and implementation discipline -
  the CEO testimonial on the live site frames this directly: "Retail
  success comes from understanding the full picture at any moment."

# **02. Ideal Customer Profile & Buying Triggers**

## **2.1 Who should care about Managerium Retail ERP**

| **Buyer / business type**            | **Primary need**                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Retail Owner / Entrepreneur**      | See sales, stock, cash and outlet performance without depending on repeated staff updates.        |
| **Retail Head / Operations Manager** | Control counters, purchase, inventory, transfers, pricing, returns and branch coordination.       |
| **CFO / Accounts Lead**              | Connect sales and purchase activity with accounting, reconciliation and financial reports.        |
| **Store Manager**                    | Run billing, returns, discounts and stock checks with a consistent operational process.           |
| **IT / Management Team**             | Secure access, scalable modules, permission control, auditability and supportable operations.     |
| **Growing Retail Chain**             | Consolidate outlet visibility, stock movement, pricing, finance and teams as the network expands. |

## **2.2 Core ICP thought**

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p><strong>When Managerium Retail ERP is the strongest
fit</strong></p>
<p>Managerium Retail ERP is strongest when a retail business has
outgrown manual tracking, isolated POS tools, spreadsheet-based
reporting or people-dependent follow-up, and now needs connected
operational control.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## **2.3 Buying triggers**

- Opening new outlets, counters or branches.

- Repeated stock mismatch, overstock, stockout, transfer confusion or
  delayed stock visibility.

- POS and accounts are disconnected, forcing finance teams to re-enter
  transactions.

- Pricing, discount, offer or return practices vary by staff or outlet.

- Management wants outlet-wise dashboards instead of end-of-day phone
  calls and manual Excel reports.

- Customer and loyalty data exists but is not being used for
  repeat-purchase insight.

- Current system cannot scale cleanly as outlets, counters, users or
  transaction volume increase.

- Need for stronger permission, audit, VAT documentation or process
  accountability.

## **2.4 Grounding in market reality**

These triggers are not abstract. The white paper's market analysis of
Bangladesh retail confirms the structural conditions that create them:
an estimated **71.72% of retail transactions remained cash-based as of
December 2024**, organised retail penetration sits at roughly **2–2.5%
of total trade**, and VAT compliance has shifted from a clerical task to
a systems-dependent one following BIN enforcement and Electronic Fiscal
Device rollout. A retailer feeling the ICP pain points above is not an
edge case - it is the market norm. Full market context is in Section 17.

# **03. Retail Problems Managerium Solves**

| **Business pain**             | **What happens**                                                                   | **Managerium response**                                                                                    |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Counter billing errors**    | Wrong price, wrong discount, slow queue, return confusion and repeated correction. | POS with barcode, discounts, offers, credit sales and return/exchange control.                             |
| **Stock mismatch**            | System stock and physical stock differ; outlet-wise stock is unclear.              | Inventory, transfers, audit setup, item-wise tracking and reporting.                                       |
| **Manual purchase confusion** | Overbuying, missed replenishment, duplicate supplier orders and delayed decisions. | Purchase dashboard, requisition/order workflow, analytics and reports.                                     |
| **Disconnected accounts**     | POS sales occur but finance later re-enters data manually.                         | Integrated accounting and auto-generated financial transaction capability in relevant plans/configuration. |
| **Multi-outlet blind spot**   | Owner cannot compare sales, stock and branch activity quickly.                     | Outlet-wise dashboards, transfers and consolidated reporting.                                              |
| **Price & discount leakage**  | Different counters use inconsistent pricing or unauthorised discounts.             | Multiple pricing, offer setup, discount management and permissions.                                        |
| **Customer data unused**      | Daily sales occur without clear loyalty or buying-pattern insight.                 | CRM, loyalty, customer analytics, basket behaviour and purchase trends.                                    |
| **Retail team complexity**    | Attendance, overtime, bonuses and salary are separate from retail operations.      | Payroll/team features in applicable scope.                                                                 |
| **Growth chaos**              | More counters/outlets increase complexity and manual coordination.                 | Modular scaling and centralised operational visibility.                                                    |

## **3.1 The strategic narrative**

<p>Begin with an operational problem the decision-maker already feels.
Explain why it happens. Show the business consequence. Then introduce
Managerium Retail ERP as the structured operating response. Close with a

# **04. Retail ERP Architecture - The Nine Layers**

Managerium Retail ERP can be understood as nine connected operating
layers. The exact feature mix depends on package and implementation
scope - see Section 13 for the package-by-package breakdown.

style="width:6.45833in;height:3.67708in" />

*The Managerium main navigation and Corporate Dashboard. The same
underlying platform and left-rail module structure powers both
Managerium ERP and Managerium Retail ERP; Retail ERP packages configure
and license a defined subset of these modules.*

| **Layer**                      | **Core scope**                                                                       | **Business value**                                    |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| **POS & Billing**              | Barcode billing, discount, offer, credit sales, returns/exchange, multi-counter.     | Fast and consistent counter execution.                |
| **Inventory & Stock**          | Item-wise stock, transfers, audits, adjustment/enterprise inventory visibility.      | Better stock accuracy and outlet control.             |
| **Purchase**                   | Dashboard, requisition/order, analytics, reports.                                    | More disciplined replenishment and supplier control.  |
| **Accounts & Finance**         | GL, AR/AP, expenses, journals, transfers, bank reconciliation, consolidated finance. | Cleaner financial management and less repeated entry. |
| **Pricing & Offers**           | Multiple price, discount, offer, VAT discount, price tag.                            | Consistent price execution across counters/outlets.   |
| **CRM & Loyalty**              | Customer/supplier management, loyalty, analytics, purchase trends.                   | Retention and customer insight.                       |
| **Payroll & Team**             | Attendance, shifts, overtime, bonuses, salary.                                       | Connects workforce operations with retail activity.   |
| **Analytics & Dashboard**      | Sales, inventory, finance, customer and management reports.                          | Faster decision-making.                               |
| **Security / Offline / Cloud** | Permissions, audit-related controls, offline capability by plan, cloud access.       | Resilience, accountability and remote visibility.     |

*This nine-layer model is the working architecture from the September
2026 overview. For the full module-by-module feature inventory at the
platform level (all fifteen top-level modules, every sub-screen), see
the Managerium ERP Master Brand & Marketing Document, Section 06 -
Retail ERP packages license a configured subset of that same inventory.*

# **05. POS & Billing**

## **5.1 What the POS layer covers**

- Barcode-based billing

- Discounts and offers

- Credit sales

- Returns and exchanges

- VAT discount support in relevant retail configuration

- Multi-counter operation

- Outlet sales reports

- Price-tag related management in higher-tier scope

## **5.2 Why it matters**

Retail operations live or die at the counter. A disconnected POS can
record a sale but still leave inventory, finance, pricing and management
reporting fragmented. Managerium Retail ERP positions POS as the
transaction front-end of a wider operating system rather than a
standalone billing tool.

<p>A POS shows the sale. A Retail ERP should show the business behind
the sale.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## **5.3 Best content angles**

- "Why sell in one software and calculate in another?"

- "Your POS is showing sales. But is it showing your business?"

- Counter-to-cloud story: every transaction should connect with stock,
  accounts and management visibility.

# **06. Inventory & Stock**

## **6.1 Inventory capabilities in Retail ERP sources**

- Basic inventory and item-wise stock visibility

- Multi-inventory / enterprise inventory tracking in higher tiers

- Stock transfer across inventories/outlets

- Audit setup and stock review

- Stock reporting and outlet-wise visibility

- Stock-related controls linked with POS and purchase activity

## **6.2 Core inventory problems**

| **Problem**            | **Retail impact**                                                                      |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Stock mismatch**     | Promised items may not be available; finance and purchase decisions become unreliable. |
| **Overstock**          | Working capital is tied up in slow-moving products.                                    |
| **Stockout**           | Lost sales and poor customer experience.                                               |
| **Branch imbalance**   | One outlet has excess stock while another faces shortage.                              |
| **Delayed visibility** | Management reacts after the problem instead of during the operational cycle.           |

# **07. Purchase Management**

## **7.1 Purchase scope**

- Purchase Dashboard

- Purchase Requisition / requisition control

- Purchase Order Management

- Purchase Analytics

- Purchase Reports / POS Purchase Report

- Receiving and supplier-facing workflow context in the broader
  Managerium ERP platform

## **7.2 Business value**

The purchase layer is meant to move retail replenishment away from
disconnected calls, manual lists and duplicate buying decisions toward a
structured purchase flow supported by inventory and purchase visibility.

| **Before**                                          | **With structured retail purchase flow**                                  |
|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Reorder depends on memory or WhatsApp messages.** | Use reports/data to identify need and start a requisition/order workflow. |
| **Duplicate or inconsistent supplier orders.**      | Keep order and purchase records inside a common process.                  |
| **Purchase information is separate from stock.**    | Connect receiving/purchase activity with inventory visibility.            |
| **Accounts team chases purchase details later.**    | Use integrated finance capability where configured.                       |

# **08. Accounts & Finance**

## **8.1 Finance capabilities**

- Auto-generated financial transactions in applicable Retail ERP scope

- Integrated accounting

- General Ledger (GL)

- Accounts Receivable / Accounts Payable (AR/AP)

- Expenses and journals

- Fund transfers

- Bank reconciliation

- Consolidated financials in higher-tier scope

- Budgeting and financial reporting

## **8.2 Core finance story**

Retail finance becomes inefficient when sales happen in POS, purchases
sit in another tool, and accounts are reconstructed manually later.
Managerium Retail ERP's finance story is strongest when positioned as a
connected transaction flow: counter and operational data should feed
finance instead of being re-entered.

structured data that finance can use.</p></td>

# **09. Pricing, Offers & Counter Control**

## **9.1 Pricing scope**

- Multiple Price Management

- Discount & Offer Management

- Customer/segment-linked pricing context

- VAT discount support in relevant retail scope

- Price Tag / Price Tag Management in higher tiers

- Multi-counter operation

- Permission-based control in the broader system

## **9.2 Why this matters**

Price leakage is not only a pricing problem; it is an operational
control problem. Different counters or outlets using inconsistent
prices, discounts or offers can create margin leakage and customer
confusion. Centralised rule-setting and permission-based execution help
standardise retail pricing behaviour.

# **10. CRM, Loyalty & Customer Insight**

## **10.1 Customer capabilities**

- Customer and supplier management

- Loyalty programs

- Discount/loyalty logic

- Advanced CRM and loyalty in higher-tier scope

- Customer analytics

- Top-customer insight

- Basket behaviour

- Purchase trends

## **10.2 Business outcome**

Retailers often collect transaction data without turning it into
customer knowledge. Managerium Retail ERP can be positioned as helping
retailers understand who buys, what they buy, how baskets behave, and
where loyalty can be used to support retention.

# **17. Bangladesh Retail Market Landscape**

This section summarises the "Re-Engineering Retail Operations in
Bangladesh" white paper (AKIJ iBOS / Managerium, 2026), which provides
the external market evidence behind the ICP pain points in Section 02
and the case studies in Section 18.

## **17.1 Market overview**

| **Metric**                                                  | **Figure**                                 | **Source**                                                       |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Wholesale & retail trade share of GDP, FY2024**           | 14.43%                                     | Economic Review 2024, cited in The Financial Express, 2024       |
| **Wholesale & retail trade share of GDP, FY2023**           | 14.42%                                     | Economic Review 2024, cited in The Financial Express, 2024       |
| **Informal employment share, Bangladesh**                   | Approximately 84.9%                        | ILO, 2025                                                        |
| **Urban population share, 2024**                            | Approximately 32.7%                        | World Bank Data, 2024                                            |
| **Organised retail (supermarket) penetration**              | Approximately 2–2.5% of total retail trade | Prothom Alo English, 2023                                        |
| **E-commerce penetration**                                  | Roughly 3–5% of total retail               | The Daily Star, 2025                                             |
| **Mobile Financial Services (MFS) transaction value, 2024** | Tk 17.42 lakh crore, up 28.53% YoY         | The Business Standard, 2025 (Bangladesh Bank data)               |
| **Cash-based transaction share, December 2024**             | Approximately 71.72%                       | The Business Standard / tbsnews.net, 2025 (Bangladesh Bank data) |

## **17.2 What this means for retail operations**

- **A small organised segment under rising compliance pressure, and a
  vast informal base with limited digitisation.** Managerium Retail ERP
  sits at exactly this transition point.

- **Retail chains cluster in Dhaka and Chattogram** due to consumer
  density, purchasing power, logistics connectivity and digital payment
  penetration - the natural first-wave geography for outbound and paid
  campaigns.

- **Digital payments are growing fast but cash still dominates.** This
  hybrid payment environment demands stronger auditability and control -
  a direct argument for POS-to-accounts integration rather than
  standalone billing.

- **VAT compliance is now systems-dependent, not clerical.** The VAT and
  Supplementary Duty Act 2012, BIN requirements, Electronic Fiscal
  Device deployment and online VAT filing mean transaction-level data
  accuracy and audit trails are increasingly mandatory - directly
  supporting the "Integrated VAT Management" add-on story in Section 12.

## **17.3 Core operational challenges (white paper Chapter 1.2)**

| **Challenge**                                   | **White paper evidence**                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **Retail consequence**                                                                                                                   |
|-------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Inventory inefficiency**                      | Manual demand forecasting, disconnected warehouses, limited real-time visibility, logistics unpredictability. World Bank logistics assessment cites high inventory carrying costs linked to congestion and supply uncertainty. | Defensive overstocking, stockouts of fast-moving SKUs, working capital pressure, perishable loss risk.                                   |
| **Supply chain & cold chain gaps**              | World Bank/IFC identify temperature-controlled logistics as critical for preserving value and reducing food loss in emerging markets.                                                                                          | Fresh category shrinkage, quality volatility, limited traceability, reduced consumer trust.                                              |
| **Fragmented operational systems & data silos** | Standalone POS, manual reconciliation, spreadsheet-based inventory, separate finance tools; cash dominance further limits digital audit trails.                                                                                | Manual end-of-day reconciliation, delayed financial closing, limited enterprise visibility, no real-time profitability analysis.         |
| **VAT compliance pressure**                     | NBR framework requires transaction-level documentation, BIN registration, electronic filing and auditable invoice trails.                                                                                                      | Non-integrated systems elevate regulatory risk; manual VAT reconciliation delays reporting; inaccurate input VAT tracking erodes margin. |
| **Scalability constraints**                     | Expansion multiplies SKU complexity, outlet coordination, VAT reporting layers, logistics dependencies and workforce management requirements.                                                                                  | Operational strain increases faster than revenue gains without structural integration, especially outside core metropolitan areas.       |

## **17.4 The white paper's ERP argument**

The white paper positions Managerium directly as the structural response
to these five challenges - not an incremental fix. Its framing:
"Managerium was designed as a unified retail ERP framework purpose-built
for the structural realities of Bangladeshi retail: high transaction
volumes, multi-outlet operations, VAT-intensive compliance requirements,
and the transition from fragmented processes to centralized governance."

It describes Managerium's integrated architecture as covering real-time
POS and inventory synchronisation, centralised procurement and warehouse
management, financial accounting with embedded VAT automation, CRM and
customer analytics, production alignment for food and perishable retail,
and multi-branch dashboards with role-based governance.

# **18. Case Studies - Managerium In Action**

Five case studies from the white paper, each reflecting a different
operational complexity but a common structural shift: moving from
fragmented processes to system-driven governance.

## **18.1 Agora Limited - Enterprise-Grade Control at Scale**

Agora operates one of Bangladesh's most established superstore networks,
managing thousands of SKUs across multiple high-traffic outlets.

**Challenge:** As outlet count expanded, disconnected systems began
creating structural inefficiencies. Inventory imbalances increased, VAT
consolidation required manual intervention, and management lacked
real-time enterprise visibility. Operational oversight was increasingly
store-dependent rather than centrally governed.

**System intervention:** Managerium was deployed as a centralised POS
solution across outlets, enabling standardised billing and real-time
sales visibility. Head office gained transaction-level oversight while
maintaining store-level speed, accuracy and operational responsiveness.

- 30% reduction in stockouts

- Faster checkout cycles and improved customer experience

- Improved sales tracking accuracy

- Enhanced transaction-level visibility across outlets

**Strategic implication:** Through standardised POS integration, Agora
strengthened transaction discipline and gained clearer sales visibility
across outlets, improving operational responsiveness and reducing manual
oversight burdens.

## **18.2 Paragon Mart - Managing Complexity in a Growing Retail Network**

Paragon Mart operates a multi-outlet grocery network, where scaling
operations increased complexity across procurement, inventory
management, production planning and reporting.

**Challenge:** Rapid expansion introduced inventory mismatches, demand
forecasting gaps and inefficiencies in production-linked replenishment.
Perishable categories faced volatility due to weak synchronisation
between retail sales and backend production planning.

**System intervention:** Managerium was deployed as a fully integrated
ERP platform encompassing POS, inventory, procurement, finance and
production modules. Real-time synchronisation aligned retail sales data
with centralised production planning and warehouse operations.

- 25% improvement in on-shelf availability

- 20% reduction in perishable waste

- Improved production-demand alignment

- Faster enterprise-level reporting and decision-making

**Strategic implication:** Through integrated ERP and production
planning, Paragon Mart achieved centralised control, stronger
operational consistency and scalable growth.

## **18.3 Prince Bazar - Eliminating Errors Through Integration**

Prince Bazar is one of the largest and longest-established superstore
chains in its region.

**Challenge:** Inventory inaccuracies, delayed financial reporting and
VAT complexity constrained scalability. Manual reconciliation consumed
managerial time and introduced avoidable errors.

**System intervention:** Managerium replaced standalone POS and manual
accounting processes with a unified ERP integrating sales, inventory and
finance. Real-time inventory tracking reduced dependency on manual
audits.

- 99%+ inventory accuracy

- Near elimination of reconciliation delays

- Automated VAT compliance

- Improved readiness for outlet expansion

**Strategic implication:** Prince Bazar shifted from operator-dependent
control to system-driven reliability, reducing operational risk while
preparing for structured growth.

## **18.4 H&C Bakery - Aligning Production with Retail Demand**

H&C Bakery operates a multi-outlet retail model supported by centralised
production. As a perishable-goods retailer, daily forecasting accuracy
directly affects waste levels and margin performance.

**Challenge:** Overproduction, demand misalignment and limited sales
visibility resulted in daily waste and inefficient raw material
planning. Production decisions were not sufficiently linked to real-time
retail data.

**System intervention:** Managerium was deployed as a fully integrated
ERP solution, aligning production planning with live retail sales and
inventory data. Demand patterns across outlets informed production
scheduling and procurement planning.

- 30% reduction in daily waste

- Improved availability of high-demand items

- Better raw material utilisation

- Strengthened operating margins

**Strategic implication:** The bakery transitioned from intuition-based
production planning to data-driven demand alignment, demonstrating ERP
relevance beyond traditional retail into production-linked models.

## **18.5 Khulshi Mart - Enterprise Discipline for Regional Retail**

Khulshi Mart is a regional supermarket expanding beyond a single outlet
into a structured retail chain.

**Challenge:** Manual inventory tracking, slow reporting cycles and
limited centralised oversight restricted expansion capability.
Management focus remained on operational firefighting rather than
strategic growth.

**System intervention:** Managerium centralised POS, inventory,
purchasing and accounting on a single integrated platform, enabling head
office oversight across outlets.

- 98% inventory accuracy

- Reduced excess stock and fewer stockouts

- Simplified VAT filing

- Instant reporting and performance visibility

**Strategic implication:** Khulshi Mart achieved chain-level operational
maturity without enterprise-level complexity, positioning it for
disciplined regional expansion.

# **19. Implementation Journey**

Retail ERP implementation should be positioned as an operational change
journey, not simply software installation.

| **Stage**                        | **What happens**                                                                                                                         |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1. Discovery**                 | Identify outlets, counters, product categories, current POS/accounting process, inventory pain and reporting needs.                      |
| **2. Package / scope selection** | Map the business to Standard, Professional, Premium or Enterprise based on outlet count, accounting, CRM, payroll and operational needs. |
| **3. Data preparation**          | Prepare product/SKU list, barcode, price list, supplier/customer data, opening stock, chart of accounts and user roles.                  |
| **4. Configuration**             | Set up outlets, counters, permissions, price/offer rules, inventory, purchase, accounting and reports.                                   |
| **5. Role-based training**       | Train cashiers, store managers, finance, operations and owner/management users.                                                          |
| **6. Pilot run**                 | Validate billing, stock, reports, offline flow and daily closing in a controlled outlet/counter.                                         |
| **7. Go-live**                   | Move live retail operations into Managerium with implementation support.                                                                 |
| **8. Review & optimise**         | Monitor reports, identify adoption gaps, refine workflows and plan upgrades/add-ons.                                                     |

# **20. Buyer Personas, Objections & Sales Enablement**

## **20.1 Persona messaging**

| **Persona**            | **Primary pain**                                                     | **Message direction**                                                            |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Retail Owner**       | Cannot see the full business picture without asking staff.           | See sales, stock, cash and outlet performance from one connected system.         |
| **Operations Manager** | Purchase, stock transfer and branch coordination take too much time. | Control operational workflows without scattered communication.                   |
| **Finance Lead**       | Sales/POS data needs manual reconciliation.                          | Connect operational transactions with accounting and reports.                    |
| **Store Manager**      | Billing, returns, discounts and stock checks create daily pressure.  | Standardise counter operations with POS, barcode, returns and stock visibility.  |
| **IT / Management**    | Needs secure access, configuration and auditability.                 | Use permissions, data security and audit-related controls to protect operations. |

## **20.2 Objection handling**

| **Objection**                            | **Response direction**                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **"We already have POS."**               | POS handles counter sales; Retail ERP connects POS with purchase, stock, accounts, pricing, CRM, payroll and analytics.                  |
| **"We are small now."**                  | Start with an appropriate plan (Standard) and scale as counters/outlets and operational needs grow.                                      |
| **"Our staff may not adopt it."**        | Use role-based onboarding and training for cashier, store manager, finance, operations and management.                                   |
| **"Internet may be unstable."**          | Source materials list basic (Standard) and robust (Premium) offline capability; confirm exact behaviour for the selected implementation. |
| **"We need Bangladesh-specific needs."** | Managerium is positioned around localised retail operations; VAT management is listed as an add-on.                                      |
| **"We only need stock."**                | Stock accuracy improves when sales, purchase, transfers and financial processes are connected rather than isolated.                      |

## **20.3 Discovery questions**

1.  How many outlets and counters are you managing today?

2.  Do sales, inventory and accounts live in separate systems?

3.  How often does physical stock differ from system stock?

4.  Can you compare outlet-wise sales and stock without calling multiple
    people?

5.  Are purchase orders, transfers and supplier payments connected with
    accounts?

6.  How are pricing, discounts and returns controlled across counters?

7.  If you open five more outlets, will the current process still work?

# **22. Competitive Context & Differentiation**

The existing Managerium master document uses a strategic
market-alternative shortlist rather than a market-share ranking.
Relevant local/global alternatives include PrismERP, PrideERP,
Southtech/EasyPOS, SAP Business One, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business
Central, Oracle NetSuite, Odoo, ERPNext, Bdtask ERP and other local ERP
alternatives.

## **22.1 Retail ERP differentiation themes**

- One connected platform across POS, stock, purchase, accounts, pricing,
  CRM, payroll and analytics.

- Bangladesh-ready operating context and accessible local
  implementation/support.

- Retail-specific depth rather than generic back-office ERP alone.

- Business-control messaging for owners/CXOs rather than feature-only
  communication.

- Scalable adoption from smaller retailers to multi-outlet and
  enterprise operations.

- Offline capability, outlet visibility, integrated accounting and
  loyalty/pricing depth in applicable packages.

# **23. Brand, Copy & Creative Direction**

## **23.1 Brand personality**

Intelligent, dependable, clear, practical, modern, confident and
solution-driven. Communication should be business-first and
owner/decision-maker friendly.

## **23.2 Language style**

- Use simple business English and natural Bangla where relevant.

- Keep familiar software terms in English when that is clearer.

- Use short sentences, active voice and benefit-led headlines.

- Explain business pain first, then operational context, Managerium's
  response and business outcome.

- Avoid clutter, slang, overpromising and inconsistent claims.

- Prefer "control", "structured", "connected", "visible", "organised"
  and concrete operational language over vague transformation slogans.

## **23.3 Visual identity**

| **Element**        | **Guideline**                                                                  |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Primary Blue**   | \#183870                                                                       |
| **Deep Navy**      | \#13264D                                                                       |
| **Digital Red**    | \#FD0000 - CTA / controlled accent only, never a background field              |
| **White**          | \#FFFFFF - primary background                                                  |
| **Light Grey**     | \#E0E0E0 - neutral division/background                                         |
| **Colour ratio**   | Approximately 60% white, 30% blue/navy, 10% red                                |
| **Marketing font** | Poppins                                                                        |
| **UI font**        | Roboto                                                                         |
| **Bangla font**    | Hind Siliguri or Ador Noirrit depending on readability                         |
| **Social format**  | 1:1 / 4:5 feed, 9:16 Reels/Stories, 16:9 video                                 |
| **Logo placement** | For AKIJ iBOS endorsed communication: AKIJ iBOS top-left, Managerium top-right |

# **24. Content Strategy & Authority Territories**

## **24.1 Recommended content mix**

| **Share** | **Content type**    | **Focus**                                                                                |
|-----------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **40%**   | Problem & Education | Stock mismatch, delayed reporting, disconnected finance, manual processes, growth chaos. |
| **25%**   | Product & Feature   | POS, modules, dashboards, workflows, offline, integrated accounting, pricing, loyalty.   |
| **20%**   | Proof & Trust       | Case studies, customer stories, support, implementation and industry adoption.           |
| **10%**   | Thought Leadership  | Business control, scaling, data-driven retail management and ERP readiness.              |
| **5%**    | Offer & CTA         | Demo, consultation, webinar or direct lead action.                                       |

## **24.2 Strong Retail ERP content territories**

- POS is not enough - billing vs full retail operations.

- Stock mismatch kills growth - system stock vs shelf reality.

- Owner visibility - if you need to call the store to know sales,
  control is weak.

- Retail chain scalability - one outlet can run on effort; ten outlets
  need a system.

- Accounting integration - why sell in one software and calculate in
  another?

- Customer loyalty and basket insight - use transaction data to
  understand repeat buyers.

- Price and discount leakage - central rules vs counter-by-counter
  variation.

- Branch stock imbalance - transfer and visibility across outlets.

- Pharmacy operational structure - branch stock, SKU, reorder review,
  pricing, purchase and finance.

- ERP implementation education - process, data and user adoption, not
  software alone.

- Bangladesh retail's cash-to-digital transition and what it means for
  reconciliation and control (grounded in the white paper's market data
  - Section 17).

## **24.3 Social narrative structure**

Hook \> Problem \> Narrative \> Solution \> CTA. For statics, the
headline should usually communicate either a concrete pain or an
immediately understandable business outcome. For carousels, build one
connected story instead of six disconnected feature cards.

# **00. Document Purpose and Usage Protocol**

This is a complete AI-feedable master product knowledge document for
Prime VAT. It is designed to become the single source of context for
anyone creating Prime VAT content, campaigns, scripts, captions,
carousel copy, static copy, website copy, sales pitch, explainer videos,
motion videos, competitive messaging and internal briefing material.

## **What This Document Should Do**

- Explain what Prime VAT is and why it matters for Bangladeshi
  businesses.

- Capture the full product structure from the landing page, user manual,
  screenshots, web portal service list and working marketing context.

- Guide any AI model to write Prime VAT content without missing core
  product features or making unsupported claims.

- Protect the brand from repetitive, generic and legally risky
  messaging.

- Give the marketing team enough detail to create static posts,
  carousels, reels, motion videos, landing pages, sales decks and
  campaign plans.

## **How an AI Should Use This Document**

- Always treat Prime VAT as a complete VAT workflow management system,
  not only a Mushak form generator.

- Use the product modules and feature inventory in this document before
  creating any claim about the product.

- Use Bangla-primary wording for local marketing content, while keeping
  technical terms such as VAT, Mushak, Invoice, Challan, VDS, Return,
  Compliance, Audit, Workflow, System and Prime VAT when natural.

- When writing public legal/compliance claims, stay within the claim
  safety rules and verification notes in this document.

- Never repeat exact carousel or static copy lines in captions unless
  explicitly requested.

- Avoid making every caption or hook sound the same. Rotate angles
  across workflow automation, challan, VDS, branch-wise control, return
  readiness, invoice control, manufacturing VAT and audit-ready records.

# **02. Executive Product Summary**

Prime VAT is a web-based VAT management software platform for
Bangladeshi businesses. It helps Finance, Accounts, VAT, Compliance and
Operations teams manage VAT records, purchase and sales data, invoices,
challan, VDS, branch-wise VAT information, Mushak forms, audit reports,
MIS reports and VAT Return preparation from one organized workflow.

The strongest strategic positioning is: Prime VAT transforms scattered
VAT work into a smart, organized and controlled VAT workflow.

## **Short Product Pitch**

Prime VAT brings daily VAT work into one structured system. From
purchase and sales to invoice, challan, VDS, branch-wise records, audit
reports and VAT Return 9.1 preparation, it helps businesses reduce
manual pressure, organize documents and keep VAT workflow easier to
control.

## **Long Product Pitch**

VAT management is not only a month-end return task. It starts from daily
purchase, sales, invoice, challan, VDS, branch operations, manufacturing
activity, stock movement and reporting. When these records stay
scattered across Excel files, manual documents and separate branch-level
records, Finance Teams face reporting delays, mismatch risk and audit
pressure. Prime VAT organizes these workflows in one platform so
businesses can manage VAT work faster, smarter and with better
operational control.

## **What Prime VAT Is**

- A VAT Management Software platform for businesses in Bangladesh.

- A system for organizing VAT workflow across purchase, sales, invoice,
  challan, VDS, branch data, reports and return preparation.

- A web-based operational system for Finance, VAT, Accounts and
  Compliance Teams.

- A tool for improving document readiness, VAT reporting visibility and
  internal control.

- A product that can be explained through workflow automation,
  compliance readiness and business control.

## **What Prime VAT Is Not**

- It should not be described only as a Mushak generator.

- It should not be described as a replacement for legal advice or a VAT
  consultant.

- It should not be marketed with unsupported guarantee claims such as
  penalty-free, 100% error-free or no audit risk.

- It should not be positioned only as a month-end return tool.

- It should not be confused with personal income tax return software.

# **05. Product Category and Market Context**

Prime VAT operates in the business VAT management, tax workflow
automation and compliance reporting category for Bangladesh. The product
should be explained for companies that need accurate records, faster
report preparation and easier VAT workflow control.

## **Core Market Reality**

- VAT work is a daily business workflow, not only a monthly return
  activity.

- Purchase, sales, invoice, challan, VDS, branch data and return
  preparation are connected in practical VAT operations.

- Manual and scattered records create delay, mismatch, repeated entry,
  document searching and reporting pressure.

- Businesses need systems that help them maintain structured records and
  generate necessary VAT documents faster.

- Finance leaders need visibility and control, while VAT teams need
  practical workflows.

## **Official VAT Context for Content**

NBR’s public VAT FAQ states that a registered person furnishes VAT
Return in Form VAT-9.1 within the 15th day of the following month of the
tax period. The NBR compliance guide also lists taxpayer
responsibilities such as asking for VAT Invoice (Mushak-6.3) during
purchase, issuing it during sales, keeping purchase and sales records
properly, paying net VAT and submitting return after each tax period,
checking VAT Online posting and complying with withholding tax
responsibility if applicable.

Use these official points as general content context only. For final
legal wording, verify with current NBR circulars, rules, SROs and
qualified tax professionals.

## **Non-Prime VAT Content Boundary**

Personal income tax return rules, bank balance tips, Statement of Assets
& Liabilities and individual taxpayer return quarter rules are not
direct Prime VAT content. They may inspire structure or style, but Prime
VAT content should focus on business VAT, Mushak, challan, invoice, VDS,
branch records, audit reports and VAT Return workflows.

# **11. Detailed Configuration Module**

The Configuration module makes the system operational by setting core
dependencies before users enter VAT operation and transaction data. It
includes business setup, tax setup, branch setup, item setup,
customer/supplier setup, user management, role management and vehicle
management.

## **Business Config**

### **Tax Config**

Tax Config maps the business with tax setup based on business structure
and trade type. The user manual notes that the system requires tax zone,
tax circle, return submission date, representative, representative
designation, representative address, BIN number, tax bracket, ownership
type, business unit address, economic activity name, VAT deduction
source tax checkbox, surcharge type and business nature.

| **Field / Setup Item**     | **Purpose**                                          |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Tax Zone                   | Select the tax zone for the business.                |
| Tax Circle                 | Select the tax circle for the business.              |
| Return Submission Date     | Set the date used for return submission workflow.    |
| Representative             | Select responsible return submission representative. |
| Representative Designation | Select the representative designation.               |
| Representative Address     | Store representative address.                        |
| BIN Number                 | Store company Business Identification Number.        |
| Tax Bracket                | Select tax bracket for the business.                 |
| Ownership Type             | Select business ownership type.                      |
| Business Unit Address      | Store business unit address.                         |
| Economic Activity Name     | Store business economic activity name.               |
| VAT Deduction Source Tax   | Checkbox if the company deducts VAT from source.     |
| Surcharge Type             | Select company surcharge type.                       |
| Business Nature            | Select the nature of the business.                   |

### **Branch**

Branch setup allows users to store branch information and VAT/TAX
configuration for a particular branch. Branch records can be created,
viewed, edited and extended.

| **Branch Field** | **Purpose**                          |
|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Branch Name      | Name of the branch.                  |
| Address          | Address of the branch.               |
| Country          | Country selection.                   |
| State / Division | State or division selection.         |
| City / District  | City or district selection.          |
| Police Station   | Police station selection.            |
| Post Code        | Auto-filled based on police station. |

## **Item Config**

### **Item Category**

Item Category stores categories based on the items used by the business.
The manual states this information is required to create items.

| **Item Category Field** | **Purpose**                                              |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| Business Unit           | Shows the business unit where item category is saved.    |
| Item Type Name          | Select item type such as Finished Goods or Raw Material. |
| General Ledger          | Select the required general ledger.                      |
| Item Category Name      | Enter the category name.                                 |

### **Unit of Measure**

Unit of Measure stores UoM information used for item creation and
business operation.

| **UoM Field** | **Purpose**                          |
|---------------|--------------------------------------|
| UoM Name      | Write the unit of measure name.      |
| Code          | Write the code for the specific UoM. |

### **Item**

Item setup stores item information according to tax types such as
Purchase Book Item, Sales Book Item and Trade Item. It supports tax
amount calculation context for item transactions and includes item type,
category, HS code and supplier type related information.

| Item Type      | Select item type such as Asset, Finished Goods, Raw Materials or Service Goods. |

Price Declaration allows the user to set price for individual items

# **16. VAT Form and Compliance Context**

This section converts VAT form and regulatory context into safe product
messaging. It should be used for authoritative content while avoiding
unsupported legal claims.

## **VAT Return 9.1 Deadline Context**

Official NBR VAT FAQ context: VAT Return in Form VAT-9.1 is submitted
within the 15th day of the following month of the tax period. If the
15th is a public holiday, the return should be furnished on the
preceding working day. Online submission can be done 24/7 according to
the NBR FAQ.

### **Prime VAT Content Angle**

- VAT Return-এর ১৫ তারিখের deadline সামনে?

- Deadline-এর আগে VAT Data গুছিয়ে রাখুন.

- Return Preparation শুরু হয় Organized Data থেকে.

## **Mushak-6.3 VAT Invoice Context**

NBR compliance guidance lists taxpayer responsibility to ask for VAT
Invoice (Mushak-6.3) during purchase and issue the same during sales.
For Prime VAT, this supports purchase-sales invoice control and
Mushak-6.3 management content.

## **Purchase and Sales Record Context**

NBR compliance guidance includes keeping purchase and sales records
properly. Prime VAT’s purchase and sales modules directly support this
messaging.

## **VDS / Withholding VAT Context**

NBR guidance and FAQ materials include withholding tax/VDS
responsibility where applicable. Prime VAT’s VDS features can be
positioned around tracking pending/completed VDS status and keeping VDS
certificate information organized.

## **NBR Rule and SRO Update Context**

NBR maintains VAT rules and VAT SRO pages with updates, amendments and
gazettes. Prime VAT marketing can say the system supports VAT-related
updates based on product team confirmation. Use safer wording such as
“NBR-এর VAT Update অনুযায়ী দ্রুত System Update সুবিধা” rather than
unsupported absolute claims.

# **20. Differentiation and Competitive Positioning**

Prime VAT should be positioned against manual VAT work, Excel-based
tracking, disconnected accounting processes and generic software that
does not give VAT teams a complete Bangladesh-specific workflow.

| **Alternative**             | **Common Problem**                                                                 | **Prime VAT Positioning**                                                    |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Manual / Paper Records      | Slow, scattered and hard to retrieve.                                              | Digital, organized and easier to access.                                     |
| Excel-based VAT Work        | Duplicate entry, formula risk, version confusion and branch mismatch.              | Structured workflow and dashboard visibility.                                |
| Generic Accounting Software | May not cover detailed VAT forms, VDS, Mushak and Bangladesh-specific VAT reports. | VAT-focused workflow for Bangladeshi compliance needs.                       |
| Disconnected Branch Files   | Head Office cannot easily view or reconcile all branches.                          | Branch-wise records and centralized reporting.                               |
| Only Form Generator         | May create forms without operational workflow control.                             | Complete VAT workflow from purchase/sales to reports and return preparation. |

## **Differentiator Statements**

- Prime VAT is a VAT workflow management system, not only a document
  generator.

- It covers daily VAT operations, not only month-end return preparation.

- It supports both data organization and reporting visibility.

- It connects purchase, sales, invoice, challan, VDS, branch and return
  contexts.

- It supports trading, service, manufacturing and multi-branch business
  contexts.

keeping purchase, sales, invoice, challan, VDS and branch records in
separate files, your Finance Team can keep VAT work organized in one
system. This helps reduce manual pressure, improve report readiness and
make VAT management easier to monitor.

Prime VAT helps Finance Teams organize VAT data across purchase, sales,
invoice, challan, VDS, branch records and return preparation. It
supports faster document preparation, branch-wise visibility,
audit-ready reporting and smoother VAT workflow control.

Prime VAT helps VAT Teams manage Mushak forms, VAT records, challan, VDS
certificates, adjustments and return data in one system. It reduces
repetitive manual checking and makes required records easier to access
when needed.

# **23. Static, Carousel, Caption and Reel Rules**

## **User-Approved Writing Preferences**

- Use premium, simple Bangla/Banglish for local content.

- Write complete and meaningful sentences, not broken fragments.

- Keep static H1 around 6 words and subheading around 7-8 words when
  requested.

- For carousel, use 4 cards: Hook, Problem, Narrative + Solution, CTA.

- Keep carousel card copy around 6-7 words unless user requests
  otherwise.

- Do not use comma breaks inside short carousel lines when user requests
  clean lines.

- Do not repeat the exact carousel/static headline in caption opening.

- Avoid repeating the same hook tone such as “Ready?”, “আছে তো?”, “এখনও
  করছেন?” across every content.

- Use Bangla bullets where possible, with English technical terms only
  when natural.

## **Caption Structure**

Captions should generally follow this order: fresh opening hook,
problem, narrative, solution, benefit bullets and CTA. The caption
should not copy the exact creative headline line.

## **Better Caption Opening Styles**

- একটা Invoice এক জায়গায় আর Challan আরেক জায়গায় থাকলেই VAT Process জটিল
  হতে শুরু করে.

- Business যখন এক Branch থেকে অনেক Branch-এ যায়, VAT কাজও তখন multiply
  করে.

- Month-end এ VAT Return বানানোর সময়ই বোঝা যায় কোন data missing.

- একই VAT Data বারবার Entry করতে করতে Finance Team-এর সময় নষ্ট হয়.

- Challan বানানো যদি এখনও manual হয়, তাহলে VAT Process ধীর হবেই.

## **Words to Use**

- VAT

- Mushak

- Invoice

- Challan

- VDS

- Compliance

- Return

- Audit

- Report

- Workflow

- System

- Management

# **27. Claim Safety, Verification and Legal Guardrails**

Prime VAT content deals with VAT, NBR, Mushak forms, challan, VDS and
compliance. Public content must be careful, accurate and not
overpromising.

## **Safe Claims**

- Prime VAT helps keep VAT records organized.

- Prime VAT helps reduce manual VAT work pressure.

- Prime VAT helps prepare necessary VAT documents faster.

- Prime VAT helps keep purchase, sales, invoice, challan, VDS and return
  data in one system.

- Prime VAT supports audit-ready documentation and reporting.

- Prime VAT helps businesses manage branch-wise VAT information.

- Prime VAT helps make VAT Return preparation easier.

- Prime VAT helps track VDS status.

- Prime VAT helps Finance Teams manage daily VAT workflow more
  efficiently.

## **Claims to Verify Before Publication**

| **Claim**                                                  | **Validation Note**                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NBR Approved / NBR Recognized                              | Landing page uses these claims. Verify certificate/status before strong public use. |
| 40% more efficiency                                        | Landing page claim. Needs methodology or approval before ad use.                    |
| Fully automated VAT calculation                            | Use with caution. User previously corrected broad automation claims.                |
| One-click NBR submission                                   | Avoid unless product team confirms actual NBR portal submission integration.        |
| Few seconds document generation                            | Use only when confirmed for the specific document.                                  |
| 3-hour implementation support                              | Working context says this; verify operationally.                                    |
| 24/7 Expert Support                                        | Working context says this; verify support availability.                             |
| NBR VAT updates quickly added to system                    | Use as support/process claim after product confirmation.                            |
| Companies above BDT 5 crore turnover must use VAT software | Manual states it; verify current rule before public legal claim.                    |
| Mushak 6.10 / 2 lakh threshold                             | Working context mentions it; verify before authoritative content.                   |

## **Preferred Safe Wording**

- Penalty Risk তৈরি হতে পারে.

- Compliance Pressure বাড়তে পারে.

- Audit Response সহজ করতে সাহায্য করে.

- VAT Records Organized রাখতে সাহায্য করে.

- Return Preparation সহজ করে.

- Manual কাজের চাপ কমায়.

- NBR-এর VAT Update অনুযায়ী দ্রুত System Update সুবিধা.
