# 110. TURBO GUARD - FULL BRAND & MARKETING REFERENCE (v1.0)

**Source note:** Appended verbatim from user-supplied `Turbo_Guard_Master_Brand_Marketing_Document_v1.0.md` (13 September 2026).

# Turbo Guard Master Brand and Marketing Document

**Brand Strategy Product Positioning Go To Market Messaging and Claims Governance**

**Version 1.0 | 13 September 2026 | Internal Master Document**

<img src="Turbo_Guard_Master_Brand_Marketing_Document_v1.0_media/media/rId20.png" style="width:1.55in;height:1.55in" alt="Turbo Guard logo" />

Turbo Guard logo

**Brand idea:** Recover the site. Recover the search presence. Stay protected.

This document is the working source of truth for Turbo Guard brand, product marketing, campaigns, sales material, website copy, WordPress.org communications, and AI-assisted content. It combines the current WordPress.org listing, internal marketing brief, USP report, product claims, visual identity evidence, and current competitor research. It distinguishes verified product facts from strategic recommendations and from claims that require validation.

The central recommendation is to avoid competing as another broad “all-in-one WordPress security” plugin. Turbo Guard should own a narrower and more commercially urgent territory: **guided WordPress recovery for site owners who need to remove malware, clear SEO spam from Google, understand what happened, and prevent recurrence without security expertise or enterprise pricing.**

# 00 How to Use This Master Document

Use this document whenever Turbo Guard content, ads, landing pages, sales conversations, product onboarding, partnerships, or visual assets are created. It is designed for leadership, product, development, marketing, design, sales, support, and AI agents.

## Source of Truth Hierarchy

| **Priority** | **Source**                                             | **Required treatment**                                                                             |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1            | Current production plugin and approved release notes   | Highest authority for what is live and how it works.                                               |
| 2            | Current WordPress.org listing                          | Publicly verifiable product, compatibility, privacy, and feature truth.                            |
| 3            | Approved commercial pricing and Freemius configuration | Authority for plans, licence limits, discounts, refunds, and renewal terms.                        |
| 4            | Approved leadership decisions                          | Authority for positioning, market focus, brand voice, and campaign policy.                         |
| 5            | Internal Turbo Guard HTML brief and USP report         | Working product and marketing evidence; conflicts must be checked against higher-priority sources. |
| 6            | This document                                          | Default strategic and messaging direction unless contradicted by newer approved evidence.          |
| 7            | Competitor websites and WordPress.org listings         | Evidence for comparison only; volatile claims must be dated and rechecked before publication.      |

## Claim Status Labels

| **Label**  | **Meaning**                                                  | **Publishing rule**                       |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Approved   | Verified in current public or internal product evidence      | May be published in normal context.       |
| Qualified  | True only under stated limits or conditions                  | Publish with the condition attached.      |
| Strategic  | Recommended positioning or future direction                  | Use as strategy, not as a technical fact. |
| Validate   | Evidence is incomplete, volatile, or internally inconsistent | Do not publish until confirmed.           |
| Prohibited | Misleading, unprovable, or strategically harmful             | Never publish.                            |

## AI and Team Non Negotiables

- Use the name **Turbo Guard** with a space and title case.
- Describe Turbo Guard as a **WordPress security and malware recovery plugin**. Do not imply it protects non-WordPress systems.
- Lead with the user outcome, not a list of security acronyms.
- Do not claim perfect security, guaranteed prevention, zero risk, zero slowdown, or 100 percent malware detection.
- Never publish “the only WordPress security plugin” unless a claim is narrowly defined, independently rechecked, and approved by legal or leadership.
- Do not say all processing is offline. Some opt-in features connect to WordPress.org, WPScan, ipapi.co, OpenAI, and Google APIs.
- Do not say no data ever leaves the server. The accurate claim is that website files are not sent to a vendor scanning cloud; specific metadata is transmitted only for documented, opt-in services.
- Keep Free and Pro boundaries explicit. Free detection and protection are broad; free cleanup is limited to three combined items.
- Treat competitor price, install count, free-tier limit, and feature availability as time-sensitive.
- Do not invent reviews, testimonials, recovery rates, scan benchmarks, customer logos, or savings.

# 01 Executive Brand Summary

Turbo Guard is a freemium WordPress security and malware recovery plugin for site owners, agencies, freelancers, and small teams. It scans site files and the WordPress database, detects malware and SEO spam, checks core-file integrity, protects login and application surfaces, and provides a controlled cleanup path with a backup before deletion. Pro adds unlimited cleanup, Live Traffic, AI Security Advisor, Geo-Fence, scheduled vulnerability scans, detailed vulnerability information, file inspection, and expanded bot protection.[^1]

The product is strongest when a user has an urgent business problem rather than an abstract interest in security: Japanese or pharma spam appearing in Google, a hacked site, suspicious files, a hosting warning, unexplained redirects, or uncertainty after a scanner reports technical findings. Turbo Guard connects four jobs that competitors often market separately: **detect the compromise, clean the site, clean the search footprint, and explain the next action.**

## Master Brand Formula

| **Element**        | **Approved direction**                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Category           | WordPress security and malware recovery plugin                                                                                                            |
| Primary audience   | Non-technical WordPress site owners with a live security or SEO-spam problem                                                                              |
| Secondary audience | Freelancers and agencies responsible for multiple WordPress sites                                                                                         |
| Core problem       | A hacked site can remain commercially damaged even after malicious files are removed because indexed spam, uncertainty, and reinfection risk remain.      |
| Core promise       | Find the threat, clean the site, clear indexed spam, and understand what to do next.                                                                      |
| Proof mechanism    | Local file and database scanning, WordPress checksum comparison, cleanup with ZIP backup, GSC cleanup, hardening, WAF, login security, and guided advice. |
| Emotional outcome  | From alarm and uncertainty to control and a clear recovery path.                                                                                          |
| Primary CTA        | Scan Your Site Free                                                                                                                                       |
| Recovery CTA       | Start Malware Cleanup                                                                                                                                     |
| Pro CTA            | Unlock Unlimited Cleanup                                                                                                                                  |

## What Turbo Guard Is Not

- Not a generic antivirus product for computers or networks.
- Not a managed security operations centre or guaranteed incident-response service.
- Not a hosting platform, CDN, backup platform, or full disaster-recovery service.
- Not only a firewall, only a scanner, or only a vulnerability notifier.
- Not a substitute for clean hosting, maintained plugins, secure credentials, backups, and professional response in complex incidents.
- Not yet a category leader by adoption or review volume; the public listing currently shows 10+ active installations and no reviews, so market trust must be earned.[^2]

# 02 Brand Foundation

## Purpose

Make WordPress security recovery understandable and accessible to people who run websites but are not security specialists.

## Vision

A WordPress ecosystem where a hacked site owner can move from detection to recovery without losing days to technical uncertainty, disconnected tools, or an unaffordable cleanup paywall.

## Mission

Build practical security tools that help WordPress owners find threats, remove them safely, repair the search impact, and strengthen the site against recurrence.

## Brand Belief

Security is not complete when a scanner finds a problem. It is complete only when the owner understands the risk, has a safe recovery path, and can restore the site’s operating and search integrity.

## Brand Values

| **Value**     | **Meaning in product and communication**                                                              |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Clarity       | Explain the threat and the next action in language a site owner can use.                              |
| Practicality  | Prioritise actions that help a user detect, clean, recover, and protect.                              |
| Control       | Keep the owner informed and provide backup, quarantine, review, and opt-in choices.                   |
| Accessibility | Keep meaningful detection and protection available without requiring an account or immediate payment. |
| Restraint     | Never create fear with exaggerated attack statistics or promise impossible security.                  |
| Transparency  | State data flows, feature limits, dependencies, and plan boundaries plainly.                          |

## Brand Archetype

**Primary archetype: The Guardian.** Turbo Guard protects a valuable asset and reduces exposure to threats.

**Secondary archetype: The Guide.** It translates findings into decisions and recovery steps rather than leaving the user with an alarming dashboard.

The Guardian must not become fearmongering. The Guide must not become patronising. The brand should feel calm in a crisis, technically capable, and action-oriented.

## Brand Personality

Calm, capable, direct, transparent, practical, and reassuring. The brand is not aggressive, hacker-themed, theatrical, or overloaded with military language.

# 03 Positioning Architecture

## Core Positioning Statement

For WordPress site owners and agencies facing malware, SEO spam, or unclear security findings, Turbo Guard is a WordPress security and recovery plugin that scans files and databases, enables safe cleanup, helps remove indexed spam through Google Search Console, and explains the next steps. Unlike security tools that stop at alerts or separate site cleanup from search recovery, Turbo Guard connects the recovery workflow in one WordPress experience.

## Unique Value Proposition

**Clean the compromise and the search damage from one recovery workflow.**

## Recommended Category Language

Use, in order of preference:

1.  WordPress Security and Malware Recovery Plugin
2.  WordPress Malware Scanner Cleaner and SEO Spam Recovery
3.  Guided WordPress Security Recovery
4.  WordPress Security Plugin for Site Owners and Agencies

Avoid making “AI security” the category. AI Security Advisor is a useful Pro feature, but the purchase is driven by recovery, protection, and clarity.

## Positioning Territories

| **Territory**              | **Strategic role**     | **Message**                                                                           |
|----------------------------|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Recovery beyond files      | Primary differentiator | Removing malware is not enough if spam pages still remain in Google.                  |
| Understand the finding     | Conversion support     | Get a plain-English explanation and numbered next steps.                              |
| Prove value before payment | Adoption wedge         | Run full detection and protection free; clean up to three items before upgrading.     |
| Local-first file privacy   | Trust wedge            | Website files stay on the site rather than being uploaded to a vendor scanning cloud. |
| Safe action                | Risk reducer           | Create an automatic ZIP backup before deletion and offer quarantine.                  |
| Agency economics           | Expansion wedge        | Multi-site pricing and recovery tools are designed for freelancers and agencies.      |

## Positioning Guardrail

Turbo Guard should not try to out-Wordfence Wordfence on threat-research scale, install base, response team, or brand authority. It should not try to out-MalCare MalCare on cloud-based automation or managed cleanup reputation. It should win a specific moment: **the owner who needs an understandable, affordable path from hacked to recovered, including the Google index.**

# 04 Audience and Ideal Customer Profile

## Primary Ideal Customer

| **Dimension**     | **Profile**                                                                                                                                       |
|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Organisation      | Small business, publisher, ecommerce store, professional service, nonprofit, creator business, or local organisation using self-hosted WordPress  |
| Team              | Owner-led or a small marketing, operations, or web team without a dedicated security specialist                                                   |
| Trigger           | Malware warning, SEO spam, suspicious redirect, host complaint, search-result pollution, vulnerable plugin alert, or a desire to improve security |
| Technical level   | Can access wp-admin and install a plugin; may not use SSH, FTP, or command-line tools                                                             |
| Buying priority   | Restore the site quickly, avoid losing traffic, understand the risk, and prevent recurrence                                                       |
| Price sensitivity | High; wants evidence before paying and prefers annual, affordable plans                                                                           |
| Trust requirement | Needs clear backup, privacy, data-flow, and compatibility information                                                                             |

## Secondary Ideal Customer

Freelancers, WordPress maintenance providers, and small agencies managing approximately 2 to 100 sites. Their needs include repeatable scans, quick cleanup, client-friendly reporting, multi-site economics, scheduled checks, and reduced time spent interpreting security alerts.

## Core Segments

| **Segment**             | **Trigger**                                                                   | **Primary message**                                                           | **Best CTA**       |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| Hacked business site    | Site is compromised or host has warned the owner                              | Find and clean critical threats with a backup-first workflow.                 | Start Free Scan    |
| SEO-spam victim         | Japanese, Chinese, Korean, pharma, casino, or other spam is visible in Google | Remove the infection and request removal of indexed spam URLs.                | Clean SEO Spam     |
| Non-technical owner     | Scanner findings are confusing                                                | See the risk and next steps in plain English.                                 | See How It Works   |
| Freelancer              | Several client sites need affordable protection                               | Use one repeatable workflow across client sites without enterprise pricing.   | Compare Plans      |
| Small agency            | Needs ongoing monitoring and response efficiency                              | Combine scheduled checks, detailed findings, cleanup, and traffic visibility. | Choose Agency Plan |
| Privacy-conscious owner | Does not want website files uploaded to a scanning vendor                     | Scan locally and control optional external services.                          | Review Privacy     |

## Anti Personas

- Enterprises that require a contracted 24-hour SOC, formal incident-response SLA, forensic certification, or cyber-insurance warranty.
- Users who expect a plugin to reverse every server, DNS, hosting, credential, or supply-chain compromise automatically.
- Non-WordPress website owners.
- Teams that will not maintain backups, updates, access control, and basic operational hygiene.
- Buyers who require independently benchmarked detection rates or certifications not yet held by Turbo Guard.

# 05 Buyer Personas and Decision Messages

| **Persona**              | **What they fear**                                         | **What they need to believe**                                    | **Best proof**                                      | **Message direction**                                               |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Business owner           | Lost sales, damaged reputation, suspension, technical cost | Recovery can start without becoming a security expert.           | Guided scan, backup-first cleanup, clear next steps | Get your site and search presence back under control.               |
| Marketing or SEO manager | Spam pages, lost rankings, blocked ads, polluted results   | Server cleanup and search cleanup can be coordinated.            | SEO-spam detection and GSC cleanup                  | The hack may be gone from the server but still visible in Google.   |

| Ecommerce operator       | Downtime, malicious redirects, checkout trust loss         | Protection covers application, login, bots, and file integrity.  | WAF, brute-force controls, 2FA, file watcher        | Protect the revenue path and recover safely when something changes. |

# 06 Jobs to Be Done

## Functional Jobs

- When my WordPress site may be hacked, help me scan files, core integrity, database content, users, and known vulnerabilities so I can identify the problem.
- When malicious files or spam content are found, help me remove or quarantine them without acting blindly.
- When spam URLs still appear in Google, help me identify and submit removal requests so search recovery can begin.
- When a technical finding appears, explain what it means and what I should do next.
- When I manage many sites, help me apply an affordable and repeatable security workflow.
- When I am not actively responding to an incident, help me harden login, application, bot, and file-change surfaces.

## Emotional Jobs

- Replace panic with a clear sequence of actions.
- Reduce fear that cleanup will break the site.
- Avoid feeling dependent on an expensive emergency service.
- Feel informed enough to explain the situation to a client, manager, or hosting provider.

## Social Jobs

- Demonstrate responsible website management.
- Reassure clients and stakeholders that the incident is being handled methodically.
- Protect professional credibility after a visible hack or SEO-spam incident.

# 08 Product Architecture

## Detect

- Full-site scanning of PHP, JavaScript, and HTML in core, content, and root paths.
- More than 30 documented malware patterns including obfuscation, common web shells, hidden iframes, malicious redirects, and spam payloads.
- Core-file integrity checking against official WordPress.org checksums.
- Database checks across posts, options, and rogue administrator accounts.
- Detection of PHP in uploads and core asset directories.
- Polyglot image backdoor detection.
- Japanese, Chinese, and Korean SEO-spam text detection.
- Vulnerability checking for WordPress core, plugins, and themes through WPScan data.

## Protect

- Application firewall controls for SQL injection, cross-site scripting, directory traversal, and PHP uploads.
- IP blocking through exact address, CIDR, range, and wildcard patterns.
- Request rate limiting.
- Brute-force protection, login logs, new-IP admin alerts, and automatic attacker blocking.
- TOTP two-factor authentication with recovery codes.
- Security headers, WordPress version hiding, user-enumeration blocking, and optional XML-RPC, REST API, and file-editor restrictions.
- Bad-bot controls for common scanners and scrapers.
- File watcher with periodic change detection.

## Clean and Recover

- Selection of critical threats for bulk action.
- Automatic ZIP backup before deletion.
- Quarantine into a protected directory.
- Free cleanup of up to three combined items.
- Pro unlimited malware and SEO-spam cleanup.
- Google Search Console connection for indexed-spam discovery, removal requests, and sitemap resubmission.

## Explain and Monitor

- Severity, path, threat name, and file-size context in findings.
- Pro file-content view before cleanup.
- Pro AI Security Advisor with attack-campaign classification and numbered next steps.
- Pro email advisory after scans.
- Pro Live Traffic with bot/human classification, 24-hour summaries, and one-click IP blocking.
- Pro Geo-Fence and trusted-location controls.
- Pro scheduled vulnerability scans and detailed CVE and fix-version information.

## Upgrade Logic

The free plan must create a complete “proof moment”: installation, scan, understandable results, and a small successful cleanup. Pro should be positioned as the plan for **scale, completeness, and recurrence** rather than as a ransom demanded at the point of panic.

Recommended upgrade sequence:

1.  User sees verified threats.
2.  User cleans up to three items with backup.
3.  Product shows remaining risk and explains the consequence of incomplete cleanup.
4.  Pro offers unlimited cleanup and ongoing monitoring.
5.  After recovery, retention shifts from emergency cleanup to scheduled protection and visibility.

# 10 Privacy Security and Data Flow Messaging

## Approved Privacy Narrative

Turbo Guard scans website files on the WordPress installation and does not upload those files to a vendor scanning cloud. External connections are limited to documented services and occur when relevant features are used or enabled.[^3]

| **Service**       | **Data sent**                            | **Trigger**                             | **Message requirement**                                                               |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| WordPress.org API | WordPress version and locale             | Integrity check or scan                 | Explain that checksums come from WordPress.org.                                       |
| WPScan            | Plugin or theme slugs and versions       | Manual or scheduled vulnerability scan  | Do not claim the vulnerability scan is completely offline.                            |
| ipapi.co          | Visitor IP address                       | Country-based Geo-Fence enabled         | State that country lookup requires IP geolocation.                                    |
| OpenAI API        | Anonymised threat-type data              | User initiates AI analysis with own key | Do not imply site content is sent. Keep “anonymised” subject to product verification. |
| Google APIs       | OAuth tokens and site URL or search data | User connects GSC and uses cleanup      | Explain that Google authorisation is user-controlled.                                 |

## Language to Use

- “Your website files stay on your server during scanning.”
- “Optional services connect only when you enable or use them.”
- “No Turbo Guard account is required for the free plugin.”
- “Review documented external services before enabling connected features.”

## Language to Avoid

- “Nothing ever leaves your server.”
- “100 percent private.”
- “Offline security.”
- “No third parties.”
- “Zero data sharing.”

# 11 Competitive Landscape

The WordPress security category is mature and crowded. Large incumbents compete on threat intelligence, install base, cloud infrastructure, managed cleanup, or broad protection. Turbo Guard cannot win by claiming a longer generic feature list. It can win by combining **affordable remediation, search-recovery workflow, local file privacy, and guidance for non-experts**.

## Competitor Roles

| **Competitor**                    | **Market position**                                 | **Principal strength**                                                                              | **Opening for Turbo Guard**                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Wordfence                         | Category authority and endpoint security suite      | Threat research, firewall, scanner, large install base, central management, incident-response tiers | Simpler recovery story, immediate free signatures, GSC recovery, backup-first cleanup, low-cost multi-site plans |
| MalCare                           | Cloud scanning and automated cleanup                | Off-site scanning, automated remediation, managed recovery plans                                    | Local file privacy, visible free scan and limited cleanup, lower cleanup entry price, GSC workflow               |
| Sucuri                            | Website security platform and cloud WAF             | Monitoring, CDN/WAF, managed cleanup and broad website coverage                                     | Native WordPress recovery UX, affordability, local scanning, SEO-spam workflow                                   |
| Kadence Security formerly iThemes | Login and hardening-led WordPress security          | User security, 2FA, brute-force controls, established ecosystem                                     | Stronger malware and SEO-spam recovery narrative                                                                 |
| All-In-One Security               | Broad free hardening and firewall toolkit           | Large feature footprint, approachable security controls                                             | Clearer incident recovery, malware cleanup, search cleanup, and guided advice                                    |
| Jetpack Protect                   | Simple vulnerability-led protection from Automattic | WPScan vulnerability database, low-friction setup, trusted ecosystem                                | Full file and database recovery workflow rather than vulnerability notification alone                            |
| Shield Security                   | Automation and reduced alert noise                  | Behavioural bot blocking, automatic response, action-first positioning                              | SEO-spam recovery, GSC cleanup, lower-complexity crisis onboarding                                               |
| SecuPress                         | Simple and performant protection                    | Usability, GDPR message, hardening and malware scanning                                             | Stronger hacked-site recovery promise and clearer multi-step cleanup story                                       |

Wordfence explicitly says free firewall rules and malware signatures are delayed by 30 days and reserves real-time updates for paid plans.[^4] MalCare’s current Protect plan excludes instant cleanup, while the Repair plan includes cleanup and begins at a materially higher price point than Turbo Guard’s internal launch pricing.[^5] Jetpack Protect focuses its free offer on daily vulnerability scans powered by WPScan rather than full incident cleanup.[^6] Shield positions around automatic blocking and reduced alert noise, creating a clear benchmark for Turbo Guard’s own “clarity over alarm” communication.[^7]

## Prohibited Competitor Claims

- “Wordfence cannot clean malware.” Its listing describes repair and deletion tools.[^8]
- “MalCare requires FTP or SSH for cleanup.” Its changelog states cleanup and restore support without FTP.[^9]
- “Turbo Guard is the only plugin that detects SEO spam.” Wordfence and other scanners also reference SEO spam.[^10]
- “No competitor supports search-engine cleanup.” Sucuri higher-tier services mention post-incident search-engine cleanup; the defensible distinction is Turbo Guard’s built-in Google Search Console workflow within the plugin experience.[^11]
- “Competitors upload all data.” Describe architecture per competitor and avoid absolute privacy attacks.

The internal source lists launch pricing of **\$16 per year for two sites, \$39.50 per year for ten sites, and \$128 per year for one hundred sites**, presented as a 60 percent launch discount. These figures must be validated against the live Freemius checkout, renewal pricing, tax handling, feature entitlements, and refund policy before public use.

## Pricing Principles

- Keep annual pricing simple and show the equivalent cost per site only when it strengthens clarity.
- Display renewal price as prominently as launch price.
- Do not compare a self-service plugin licence with a managed incident-response service as if both products provide identical labour or SLA.
- Use savings comparisons only against like-for-like capabilities and current list prices.
- Avoid “95 percent cheaper” unless the comparison method, plan scope, and date are shown.
- Use a refund period only after confirming the Freemius configuration.

## Recommended Commercial Message

**Start with a full scan and meaningful protection for free. Upgrade when you need unlimited recovery, deeper visibility, and ongoing automation.**

# 15 Messaging Pillars

## Pillar 1 Recover Beyond the Server

**Problem:** Malware may be removed while spam pages remain indexed and visible.

**Promise:** Connect site cleanup with a Google Search Console recovery workflow.

**Proof:** SEO-spam detection, indexed URL discovery, bulk removal requests, and sitemap resubmission.[^12]

**Message examples:**

- The malware may be gone. The spam can still be in Google.
- Clean the site. Then clean the search footprint.
- Recovery is not finished while hacked pages remain indexed.

## Pillar 2 Act Without Security Expertise

**Problem:** Findings use technical language but give little operational direction.

**Promise:** Prioritise risk and explain the next steps in plain English.

**Proof:** Severity-led results and Pro AI Security Advisor.

**Message examples:**

- Do not just find the threat. Understand the next move.
- From security alert to a clear recovery plan.
- See what happened, why it matters, and what to do next.

## Pillar 3 Clean with a Safety Net

**Problem:** Owners fear that deleting a flagged file will break the site.

**Promise:** Back up before deletion and provide quarantine or inspection options.

**Proof:** Automatic ZIP backup, quarantine, and Pro file-content view.

**Message examples:**

- Clean critical files without deleting blind.
- Backup first. Remove second.
- A safer path from detection to action.

## Pillar 4 Prove It Before Paying

**Problem:** Many owners discover cleanup limits only after a scan.

**Promise:** Offer full detection, meaningful protection, and limited cleanup before upgrade.

**Proof:** Free scan and protection feature set plus three-item cleanup.

**Message examples:**

- Scan the whole site. Clean the first threats free.
- See the problem before choosing a plan.
- Protection first. Upgrade when recovery needs scale.

## Pillar 5 Keep File Scanning Local

**Problem:** Security scans can require site data to move to a vendor cloud.

**Promise:** Scan website files on the WordPress installation.

**Proof:** Public privacy disclosure.[^13]

**Message examples:**

- Your website files stay on your server during scanning.
- Local file scanning. User-controlled connected services.
- Security visibility without uploading the site to a scanning cloud.

## Pillar 6 Agency Ready Economics

**Problem:** Per-site or per-incident security costs reduce maintenance margins.

**Promise:** Provide practical multi-site licensing for freelancers and agencies.

**Proof:** Proposed 10-site and 100-site tiers, subject to commercial validation.

**Message examples:**

- One repeatable recovery workflow across client sites.
- More sites. Predictable annual security cost.
- Turn client security emergencies into a standard process.

# 19 Brand Identity System

## Logo Meaning

The approved blue mark combines a shield and a rocket. The shield communicates protection; the rocket connects Turbo Guard to the broader Turbo product family and signals speed, forward movement, and recovery. The mark should be described as protection with momentum, not as a promise of faster website performance.

## Logo Usage

- Use the supplied blue logo as the authoritative mark.
- Keep the shield upright and preserve its proportions.
- Do not recolour individual shield or rocket layers independently.
- Do not add lock icons, hacker silhouettes, flames, warning tape, or extra security symbols around the logo.
- Use the mark on white, very pale blue, or deep navy surfaces with sufficient contrast.
- Keep clear space around the mark equal to at least one quarter of the shield width.
- For small favicons, use the shield and rocket mark only. For banners and documents, pair it with the Turbo Guard name.
- A formal vector master, monochrome version, and horizontal wordmark remain required.

# 20 Visual Creative Direction

## Core Visual Principle

Show the recovery workflow, not a vague cyber-security atmosphere. The foreground should present an actual WordPress problem, a Turbo Guard interface, a search-result consequence, or a clear before-and-after state.

## Recommended Creative System

| **Content type**  | **Visual focus**                                           | **Composition**                                                          |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Pain point static | Spam result, redirect, host warning, critical file finding | One large consequence, short headline, small product proof               |
| Feature static    | Scanner, GSC cleanup, backup, AI Advisor, Live Traffic     | Clean product UI on white or pale blue with one highlighted action       |
| Carousel          | Problem to recovery sequence                               | Card 1 hook, card 2 consequence, card 3 Turbo Guard workflow, card 4 CTA |
| Comparison        | One defensible feature gap                                 | Neutral table, dated source note, no competitor ridicule                 |
| Agency creative   | Multiple site cards and predictable plan                   | Portfolio view, operational consistency, economics                       |
| Tutorial          | Screenshot-led numbered actions                            | High legibility, no decorative clutter                                   |

## Image Rules

- Prefer white or pale-blue backgrounds and deep-blue type.
- Keep one strong focal point and no more than three supporting UI elements.
- Product screenshots must be current and readable.
- Red is reserved for threats and should occupy a small percentage of the composition.
- Use subtle depth and glow from the logo language, but avoid heavy glassmorphism that reduces technical credibility.
- Never fabricate scan results that look like customer evidence.
- Label illustrative data as demo data.

# 26 Landing Page Architecture

## Recommended Page Sequence

1.  **Hero:** Exact incident, recovery promise, Free limit disclosed nearby, primary CTA.
2.  **Visible problem:** Show how a hacked site affects files, database, and Google results.
3.  **Recovery workflow:** Scan → Review → Backup → Clean → GSC cleanup → Protect.
4.  **Product proof:** Current screenshots and annotated actions.
5.  **Why Turbo Guard:** GSC recovery, local file scanning, guidance, backup-first action, free proof.
6.  **Free versus Pro:** Transparent entitlements and cleanup limit.
7.  **Competitive context:** Neutral comparison with dated sources.
8.  **Privacy and compatibility:** Data-flow summary and tested integrations.
9.  **Pricing:** Launch and renewal terms, site counts, refund policy.
10. **FAQ:** Safety, performance, conflicts, Google timing, complex incidents.
11. **Final CTA:** Match the visitor’s intent.

## Hero Recommendation

**Headline:** Clean WordPress Malware and Indexed SEO Spam

**Subhead:** Scan files and databases, remove critical threats with a backup-first workflow, and use Google Search Console cleanup to address spam URLs that remain indexed.

**Primary CTA:** Scan Your Site Free

**Microcopy:** Full detection and protection are free. Cleanup is limited to three items; Pro unlocks unlimited cleanup.

# 27 Sales Enablement

## Thirty Second Pitch

Turbo Guard is a WordPress security and malware recovery plugin for site owners and agencies. It scans files and databases, checks WordPress integrity, protects login and application surfaces, and helps users clean threats with an automatic backup. Its strongest distinction is recovery beyond the server: it includes a Google Search Console workflow for indexed SEO spam and Pro guidance that explains findings in plain English.

## Discovery Questions

- What made you suspect the site was compromised?
- Is the problem visible on the website, in Google results, in hosting alerts, or in all three?
- Have malicious files already been removed?
- Do spam URLs remain indexed?
- How many WordPress sites are you responsible for?
- Which security plugin or service is already installed?
- Do you need self-service software or managed incident response?
- What access do you have: wp-admin, hosting panel, FTP, SSH, and Search Console?
- Is there a recent clean backup?

## Recommended Demo Flow

1.  Run a scan on a safe demonstration site with seeded demo findings.
2.  Show severity, path, threat category, and integrity evidence.
3.  Show backup-before-delete and quarantine.
4.  Demonstrate SEO-spam detection across file and database locations.
5.  Show the GSC cleanup flow using demo data.
6.  Show AI Advisor as explanation, not as the detection engine.
7.  Close with Free versus Pro and site-count economics.

# 28 Trust and Proof Roadmap

Turbo Guard’s largest current weakness is not feature coverage; it is trust evidence. A new security plugin with 10+ active installations and no public reviews must prove safety and competence before aggressive paid acquisition can scale.[^14]

## Priority Proof Assets

| **Priority** | **Asset**                               | **Why it matters**                                                               |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1            | Independent code and security review    | Reduces fear of installing a new security plugin.                                |
| 2            | Cleanup backup and restore test report  | Validates the highest-risk action.                                               |
| 3            | Performance benchmark                   | Replaces unsupported “no slowdown” claims with measured evidence.                |
| 4            | Compatibility matrix                    | Supports the alongside-other-plugins strategy.                                   |
| 5            | Detection test methodology              | Gives context to pattern and checksum coverage without false superiority claims. |
| 6            | Five detailed recovery case studies     | Connects technical actions with business outcomes.                               |
| 7            | WordPress.org reviews                   | Builds marketplace trust and conversion.                                         |
| 8            | Transparent security disclosure process | Signals maturity and responsible development.                                    |
| 9            | Public documentation and status history | Helps technical evaluators verify reliability.                                   |
| 10           | Data-flow diagram                       | Supports local-first privacy positioning.                                        |

## Case Study Template

Document the trigger, site type, visible symptoms, affected locations, scan findings, cleanup actions, backup mechanism, GSC actions, time to containment, time to indexed-spam decline, recurrence checks, and customer-authorised quote. Never publish client domains or screenshots without permission.

# 32 Claims Governance

## Approved or Qualified Claims

| **Claim**                                         | **Status**                           | **Required qualifier or evidence**                                             |
|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Full-site malware scan                            | Approved                             | Define supported file types and paths as listed.                               |
| Detects 30+ malware patterns                      | Approved                             | Keep pattern library documented and versioned.                                 |
| Checks core files against WordPress.org checksums | Approved                             | Internet or cached checksum dependency applies.                                |
| Scans files through chunked AJAX                  | Approved                             | Do not translate into an absolute performance promise.                         |
| Handles sites with 10,000+ files                  | Qualified                            | Validate across hosting environments before paid-media emphasis.               |
| Free cleanup of three items                       | Approved                             | State combined file or spam-item rules clearly.                                |
| Automatic ZIP backup before deletion              | Approved                             | Document storage, retention, and restore path.                                 |
| Website files stay on the server during scanning  | Approved                             | External metadata services must be disclosed separately.                       |
| Runs alongside popular security plugins           | Qualified                            | Say whitelisting reduces false positives; avoid universal no-conflict promise. |
| GSC bulk removal workflow                         | Approved                             | Google controls processing and final index state.                              |
| AI explains threats in plain English              | Qualified                            | Output quality varies; it is guidance, not guaranteed expert advice.           |
| No account required                               | Approved for free plugin             | Connected services may require their own accounts or credentials.              |
| No telemetry                                      | Approved only while technically true | Any future analytics change requires disclosure and document update.           |

## Claims Requiring Validation

- “Negligible firewall overhead.”
- “Fastest path to recovery.”
- “Zero-risk add-on.”
- “Detection is not signature-delayed” if signature updates or releases are not continuously verified.
- “Unlimited sites” where a public FAQ conflicts with internal Pro site-based licences.
- “60 percent off” without a real, established reference price and renewal disclosure.
- Any numerical cost comparison with competitors.
- Any statement that Google Ads access or organic rankings will be restored.
- Any statement that Turbo Guard detects more malware than another plugin.

## Prohibited Claims

- 100 percent secure.
- Guaranteed malware removal.
- Guaranteed no reinfection.
- Guaranteed no performance impact.
- Guaranteed ranking recovery.
- The only WordPress security plugin.
- Replaces a security professional in every incident.
- Certified, audited, enterprise-grade, or compliant without the named evidence.

# 35 Master Strategic Recommendation

Turbo Guard should enter the market through the urgent recovery problem, not through the broad promise of “more WordPress security features.” The strongest message is that a compromise has two surfaces: the site itself and the public search footprint it leaves behind. Turbo Guard can help users scan and clean the first, address the second through Google Search Console, understand the risk, and strengthen the site afterward.

The brand should therefore be built around **complete, understandable recovery**. “Complete” must remain carefully qualified: Turbo Guard provides a connected self-service workflow, not a guarantee of forensic remediation or ranking restoration. “Understandable” should be visible in product language, onboarding, reports, and campaigns, not confined to the AI feature.

The immediate commercial priority is proof. Improve the WordPress.org presentation, validate cleanup safety and performance, document compatibility and data flows, earn genuine reviews, and publish incident-led content. Once trust improves, Turbo Guard can scale high-intent search acquisition and agency plans from a differentiated position rather than compete in generic security advertising.

# 36 Source Notes and Research Limitations

This document uses product information available on 13 September 2026. Competitor features, pricing, install counts, and plan structures change frequently and must be rechecked before external comparison campaigns. The user-supplied WordPress search URL is a discovery page rather than a controlled competitor list; the working set therefore prioritises established and strategically relevant WordPress security plugins identified through the directory and their official product pages.

The supplied blue raster logo was inspected. Exact vector colour tokens, typography rules, wordmark construction, and minimum-size specifications were not supplied; the visual system in this document is a recommended working system and is marked provisional where appropriate.

The internal HTML and USP PDF are detailed but contain claims that conflict with current public competitor information or with Turbo Guard’s own public FAQ. Those conflicts have been corrected or flagged rather than repeated. In particular, Wordfence publicly describes repair and delete tools, MalCare describes cleanup without FTP, Sucuri offers search-engine cleanup in some service tiers, and Turbo Guard’s “no per-site fees or licence limits” FAQ needs reconciliation with internal site-count pricing.[^15][^16][^17][^18]
